Coding4Games has three defining features: 1) Diverse Modern Games, covering 15 games with diverse visual, strategic, and control demands; 2) Development-Test Separation, in which a coding agent uses a sandbox and the standard player interface to iteratively develop a program, after which the selected program is frozen and independently tested without language-model inference; and 3) Outcome and Process Evaluation, which measures not only game performance and reliability but also how agents use feedback, revise programs, and resolve problems during development. Across 15 games, the best program per game outscores the strongest GUI baseline on 13 and ties it on one. The human player outscores all agents on 10 games. We additionally examine the effects of development budgets. Coding4Games evaluates whether coding agents can turn their understanding of complex interactive environments into programs that work reliably on their own.

title: Visual Thinking: Training-Free Active Perception for Counting and Localizing Hard-to-Find Objects
authors: Emil Kielar, Pratik Chaudhari
abstract: Vision foundation models can precisely segment objects based solely on a text prompt. However, they struggle to recover objects that are small, occluded or whose appearance is poorly captured by the original textual description. Vision language models can examine the image and its context, they can propose richer descriptions of the objects to be detected. But these models struggle with precise segmentation and localization. We introduce Visual Thinking, a training-free framework that combines a vision-language model with Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3) through an iterative active perception loop. At each iteration, the VLM proposes short noun phrases using the image, candidate crops and history from past iterations. A controller ranks these phrases using embedding similarity between the original prompt and the proposal, an entropy-based verification priority and the novelty of the prompt. Next, SAM 3 uses prompts to detect objects in the image. We associate detections across iterations and update each object's confidence score using a weighted mean of scores obtained from SAM 3 with a larger weight for detections using narrower prompts. We supply confident detections as positive visual exemplars for SAM 3, and incorporate image tiling to recover small objects in cluttered images. We evaluate counting and localization on CARPK, FSCD-147, PixMo-Count, and OmniCount (Fruits). Compared with SAM 3, Visual Thinking reduces the counting mean absolute error (MAE) by about 18 on FSC-147 and about 8 on CARPK. It improves box average precision (AP) by more than 12 on FSCD-147 and CARPK. Visual Thinking, with fixed or no tiling, performs on par with Claude Opus 5.5 at extra-high reasoning effort, while running on single desktop GPU in about 5.91 seconds per image, compared to about 46.53 seconds per image for Claude through its API.

title: Predict Backbone, Graft Dynamics: A Decoupled Paradigm for Time Series Forecasting
authors: Lin Zhang, Zilin Li, Jingmei Zhao, Jiayang Wu
abstract: Modern long-term forecasters are typically optimized for point-wise accuracy, which rewards dominant low-frequency backbones but often suppresses high-utility local dynamics such as abrupt variations, transient surges, and turning points. We propose Predict Backbone, Graft Dynamics, a decoupled forecasting paradigm that separates stable structural prediction from grounded dynamic restoration. We instantiate it as GRAFT, where a base forecaster predicts the reliable trajectory backbone, and a dedicated grafting path restores historically recurrent dynamics through retrieval-based evidence, phase-aware release, channel-wise control, and restoration-cooperative optimization. Unlike generic post-hoc revision methods that correct residual errors, GRAFT formulates the second stage as grounded dynamic grafting, where historical response evidence is calibrated into transferable dynamics and selectively grafted onto the backbone under phase-, channel-, and confidence-aware constraints. Across the full evaluation grid of seven benchmarks, two metrics, four horizons, and six backbones, GRAFT improves over the corresponding backbone in 87% of all comparisons, with average MSE/MAE reductions of 4.6%/3.9%. Dynamic-window analyses show that GRAFT restores local dynamics while preserving the stable backbone structure. These results suggest a new principle for high-utility forecasting: predict the backbone, then graft the dynamics.

title: DexOPD: Dual-Extrapolation On-Policy Distillation for Diffusion Models
authors: Yunchao Ke, Yanzhe Hu, Yi Yang, Jiachun Jin, Zhihong Liu, Zhijie Deng
abstract: Flow-based diffusion models have become a mainstream paradigm for text-to-image generation, where task-specific post-training produces specialist models with complementary strengths. Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (OPD) offers an efficient way to consolidate these specialists into a single unified student. Recent methods strengthen supervision through teacher extrapolation, constructing stronger proxy teachers that allow distilled students to surpass the original specialists. However, their extrapolation directions remain defined solely by frozen teacher and reference models, leaving the student's own training progress unexploited. To address this limitation, we introduce DexOPD, a dual-extrapolation on-policy distillation method for diffusion models. DexOPD retains extrapolated teacher supervision while leveraging a lagging historical student as the reference for student self-extrapolation. Sampling across multiple self-extrapolation gains from shared initial noise broadens exploration along the student's evolving trajectory, and task rewards convert pairwise differences in candidate quality into a normalized auxiliary regression direction. Empirically, we evaluate DexOPD on GenEval, OCR, and DrawBench. The resulting unified SD3.5-Medium student achieves a GenEval reward of 0.9736, an OCR score of 0.9515, and a DrawBench Aesthetic score of 6.4875, surpassing the corresponding specialist teachers as well as all evaluated OPD and multi-task reinforcement learning baselines across these three benchmarks while preserving standard single-model inference.

title: Audits Need Access, Data, and Compute. But How Much?
authors: Salil Goyal, Sarah H. Cen, Daniel E. Ho
abstract: AI audits have garnered significant attention in recent months, as the ability to test and monitor AI models plays a crucial role in safe development and deployment. However, AI audit success hinges on an auditor's authority; in particular, what information and resources they have at their disposal. Ongoing debates have surrounded the question: How much model access is needed to conduct an AI audit? Auditors seek more model access, while companies resist it for reasons related to confidential business information (trade secrets) and privacy. This tug-of-war remains unresolved. Further, this debate misses a related question: How much data and compute do auditors need? In this work, we systematically investigate both questions. We provide a framework that varies each of these three dimensions-model access, data, and compute-and measures their joint effect on audit success. We apply this framework to three tasks. We find that (1) some model access is important, but there can be diminishing returns; (2) data and compute matter more for traditional fairness audits, but model access matters more for manipulation and lie detection; and (3) these three resources can be fungible (i.e., an exchange rate exists between them), meaning that model access is not the only salient factor. These results suggest that audit governance should jointly consider different dimensions of auditor authority (including model access, data, and compute) in relation to audit objectives. These issues are particularly salient as we consider the spectrum of auditing setups, from a small ecosystem of embedded evaluators with significant access to a large body of third-party auditors with greater independence but limited access. Our framework serves as a template that can be applied to different audit tasks and inform the degree of auditor authority.

title: Sounding the Black Box: Online Training of Embedded Neural Networks in Forward-Only Physical Simulators
authors: Ruiqi Shu, Tianrun Gao, Haomin Wen, Xiaomeng Huang
abstract: Hybrid physics-neural simulators embed neural networks in partial differential equation (PDE) solvers to model unresolved subgrid dynamics while preserving resolved physics and conservation laws. Because closure outputs feed back across time steps, single-step offline regression does not directly minimize multi-step rollout error, motivating online trajectory optimization. Solver backpropagation through time (BPTT) is the standard online solution when solver derivatives are available, yet many operational Fortran and C/C++ simulators expose only non-differentiable, forward-only interfaces. We introduce FORGE (Forward-Only Response and Gauss-Newton Estimation), an online framework that trains embedded networks from forward runs alone by decoupling exact network derivatives from black-box simulator dynamics. Stage I warms up the rollout via a low-dimensional Gauss-Newton step along output-orthonormal weight directions, canceling multi-layer feature drift via a final-layer correction. Stage II perturbs spatial output fields to fit a gain-bounded causal linear response operator across rollout steps, solves for regularized target outputs, and updates all weights via network backpropagation. Across five 2D and 3D benchmarks spanning phase separation, reaction-diffusion, fluid and MHD turbulence, and ocean circulation, FORGE outperforms gradient-free, reinforcement-learning, and emulator-based baselines, cutting coarse-solver test mean squared error (MSE) by 50%-96% in 2D and 70% in 3D, outperforming the strongest forward-only baseline by 16%-69%, and recovering 88%-98% of Solver BPTT's gains. Code is available at https://github.com/ChiyodaMomo01/FORGE.

title: Typical-query energy figures mislead institutional AI electricity demand
authors: Nathan Garland, Ryan Heneghan
abstract: Institutions increasingly buy large language model services, yet we still often estimate electricity use as single Wh-per-query value. We present the Surrogate Large Language Energy Emulator (SULLEE), an open bottom-up model linking token geometry, serving hardware, and workflow structure to annual institutional electricity, with uncertainty propagated by Monte Carlo simulation. When an institution multiplies a single reported "typical" per-query energy figure by its count of visible user prompts our modelling implies that this compounds two separable shortfalls: a right-skewed task-energy distribution not represented by any single scalar, and workflow amplification of each visible prompt into additional agent and tool calls. Together these imply an underestimate of total inference electricity by a factor of approximately 3.4 under present-day observed use, rising to approximately 15 under a 2030 high-integration scenario. Using Australian public universities as a case study, we show how the top 10% of highest-energy requests contributes over half of modelled institution-level energy use. We quantify how institution-level electricity demand may increase across three AI integration scenarios of: 1) a continuation of estimated present-day 2026 usage; 2) a high-uptake present-day 2026 institution, and 3) a potential 2030 uptake scenario - based on present trends of generative AI tools and their uptake. For a representative Australian university, mean annual electricity demand for AI inference purposes is projected to increase from 17.3 MWh (with a 3.1-47.1 MWh uncertainty, within P05-P95 scenario quartile ranges) under the 2026 observed-use scenario to up to 287.4 MWh (41.5-830.7 MWh) by 2030.

title: Antiferroelectric Fluids with Hierarchical Polar Organization
authors: Hiroya Nishikawa, Hina Saito, Tetsu Katayama, Atsuko Nihonyanagi, Dennis Kwaria, Hiroyuki Inuzuka, Junxi Liu, Go Watanabe, Fumito Araoka
abstract: The discovery of the ferroelectric nematic (NF) phase has accelerated research on fluids exhibiting polar order along the molecular long axis. However, their antiferroelectric (AFE) counterparts remain less explored. Here, we investigate how terminal alkyl-chain elongation competes with polar core-core interactions in a homologous series. This series exhibits modulated AFE order accompanied by SmC-type cybotactic correlations, with the AFE phase persisting in homologs bearing terminal alkyl chains of up to 17 carbon atoms. Three distinct phase sequences on cooling lead to two types of two-dimensional (2D) AFE lattices. Multiple sharp X-ray diffraction (XRD) peaks reveal rectangular and oblique lattice structures, supporting their classification as AFE columnar phases. XRD analysis and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations support a hierarchical structural model in which locally aligned polar molecules occupy thin segments of finite width within polar columns. The columns occupy the sites of a 2D lattice, with neighboring columns polarized in opposite directions. This model provides a structural framework for understanding the distinct precursor phase sequences and links packing between columns to the resulting AFE superstructures.

title: VLG-Drive: Unifying Vision-Language and Geometric Priors for Autonomous Driving
authors: Junge Zhang, Jie Zhu, Yanqi Jia, Xiangyu Xu, Zixun Huang, Wenbin He, Xin Li, Jiachen Li, Liu Ren
abstract: A driving planner needs both scene semantics, which vision-language models (VLMs) provide, and spatial structure, which geometric foundation models recover from visual history. We present VLG-Drive, which keeps both models frozen and trains only a fusion interface and a planner from trajectory labels. At each camera-grid cell, the interface fuses the paired VLM and geometry features into one joint token through a geometry-anchored residual, and a command-conditioned planner reads these tokens to predict the ego trajectory. VLG-Drive achieves 31.78 EPDMS on NavHard under perturbed initial states, the highest among the compared methods, and 88.27 PDMS on NavTest from cameras alone. Pointwise fusion outperforms independent VLM and geometry streams on both benchmarks. In closed-loop driving on 420 HUGSIM scenarios, VLG-Drive outperforms all compared planners. These results indicate that a lightweight planner trained on fused features of frozen vision-language and geometric foundation models is an effective alternative to adapting either model for planning.

title: DraftKV: Protecting Persistent Worlds through Hierarchical Streaming Retrieval
authors: Xiaoling Zhou, Haopeng Li, Yufa Zhou, Rui Ding, Yu Li, Jun Lin, Enze Xie, Chunhua Shen, Xuan Shen
abstract: Interactive video world models enable action- and camera-controlled exploration, yet struggle to maintain consistent spatial geometry and appearance when revisiting previously explored locations. Historical KV caches help auto-regressive video diffusion models maintain long-term consistency, but their retrieval and attention computation introduce substantial latency as history grows. We propose DraftKV, a training-free framework that retrieves historical KV caches based on geometric grounding and query-conditioned relevance, while combining CPU offloading with tile-wise streaming attention to reduce GPU memory usage and inference latency. Theoretically, we show that draft relevance reproduces the mean branch of full-resolution block relevance exactly, so its deviation is confined to the $β$-weighted max branch, and we bound retrieval utility loss in terms of the measured Top-K selection overlap. We further show that draft relevance cannot distinguish blocks with similar pooled descriptors regardless of camera pose, motivating geometric grounding before refinement. Then, we introduce streaming CG-Attention, which overlaps CPU-to-GPU KV transfers with attention computation through tile-wise streaming, hiding transfer latency while maintaining bounded GPU memory usage. Experiments across diverse model families show that DraftKV achieves superior generation quality and consistency while achieving $3.27\times$ end-to-end speedup and 42.2% peak GPU memory reduction over other CPU-offloaded KV cache retrieval methods. Notably, DraftKV enables high-quality interactive world generation with historical KV retrieval on a single H100 GPU using SolarWM-33B.

title: Global full-f gyrokinetic analysis of energetic-particle-driven Alfvén eigenmodes and their phase-space drive with GYSELA
authors: S. Raj, Y. W. Cho, Z. S. Qu, G. Brochard, L. Bramucci, P. Donnel, R. Bigué, M. Go, S. Mazzi, G. Dif-Pradalier, D. Zarzoso, K. Obrejan, V. Grandgirard, Y. Sarazin, K. Lim, X. Garbet
abstract: We investigate the linear stability of energetic-particle (EP) driven Alfvén eigenmodes and the wave-particle interaction in phase space, using the newly implemented energetic-particle module in the electromagnetic global full-f gyrokinetic code GYSELA. The coupled gyrokinetic-Maxwell system self-consistently evolves the EP species alongside thermal ions and kinetic electrons, retaining finite-orbit-width and global profile effects. To mitigate the relaxation of the initial distribution in global full-f models, a canonical Maxwellian initialisation is employed, which strongly reduces this relaxation and the associated change of the drive. The framework is verified against the ITPA-TAE and the reversed-shear NLED-AUG cases, including scans in EP temperature and density. The agreement with published multi-code results is quantitative for the ITPA-TAE case and qualitative for the NLED-AUG case, where a reversed-shear Alfvén eigenmode (RSAE) is found near $q_{\rm min}$. Beyond verification, we use a constants-of-motion (CoM) diagnostic to project the gyrocentre distribution and the local wave-particle power exchange ($P = -\mathbf{J}\cdot\mathbf{E}$) onto invariant space. This identifies the orbit classes and resonances that interact with the mode. For the ITPA-TAE, deeply co-passing orbits dominate the drive. For the NLED-AUG RSAE, counter-passing orbits drive the mode and co-passing orbits damp it, and the sign of the exchange follows that of the linear EP drive. These results provide a basis for future global full-f studies of nonlinear energetic-particle transport and mode saturation.

title: The Eclipsing $γ$ Doradus Star VZ Canum Venaticorum
authors: Jae Woo Lee
abstract: We present a detailed analysis of the eclipsing binary VZ CVn using TESS Sectors 50 and 77 photometry together with published spectroscopic results. The TESS light curves were modeled to refine the binary parameters, and the residual light curves were analyzed to investigate the pulsational properties of the system. We derive masses and radii of $M_{\rm A}=1.526\pm0.005$ $M_\odot$ and $R_{\rm A}=1.638\pm0.023$ $R_\odot$ for the primary and $M_{\rm B}=1.259\pm0.005$ $M_\odot$ and $R_{\rm B}=1.133\pm0.016$ $R_\odot$ for the secondary. Comparison with PARSEC evolutionary models suggests a near-solar metallicity of $Z=0.017$ and an age of 1.0 Gyr. Separate frequency analyses of the two TESS sectors reveal four signals with possible counterparts in both sectors. Two of these frequencies, $f_2=4.7486$ day$^{-1}$ and $f_6=7.1242$ day$^{-1}$, are consistent with the fourth and sixth orbital harmonics, respectively, suggesting an orbital origin rather than independent $δ$ Sct pulsations. The dominant frequency $f_1=1.7577$ day$^{-1}$ has a pulsation constant of $Q_1=0.336$ day, consistent with a $γ$ Dor-type g-mode pulsation. The weaker signal $f_5=1.9754$ day$^{-1}$ also has a pulsation constant of $Q_5=0.299$ day, although its detection remains tentative because of its low S/N. Together with the physical and evolutionary properties of the primary, these results support its classification as a $γ$ Dor pulsator rather than the previously proposed $γ$ Dor--$δ$ Sct hybrid pulsator.

title: Linear-Quadratic Graphon Mean-Field Games in Hilbert Spaces and Applications
authors: Zhen Wu, De-xuan Xu
abstract: This paper investigates a class of linear-quadratic graphon mean-field games (LQ-GMFGs) in Hilbert spaces, where heterogeneous agents are distributed over large networks. A distinguishing feature of our model, compared with the model of well-studied finite dimensional LQ-GMFGs, is that the dynamics of agents are governed by infinite dimensional stochastic evolution equations (SEEs) involving an unbounded operator. The diffusion coefficients are allowed to depend on the state, the control, and the weighted state-average. In addition, the parameters in cost functionals could be indefinite. As the number of agents, $N$, tends to infinity, following the Nash certainty equivalence methodology, the solvability of the limit GMFG is reduced to that of an operator-valued Riccati equation and a GMFG equation system. The existence of a strongly regular solution to the former is characterized by an equivalent, easily verifiable condition, and the sufficient conditions are established for the solvability of the latter by applying the spectral decomposition method. Therefore a Nash equilibrium for the limit game is obtained. Under some adequate convergence assumptions, a set of decentralized strategies for the $N$-agent game is designed based on the Nash equilibrium of the limit GMFG, and the obtained strategy profile is shown to constitute an $ε$-Nash equilibrium. Finally, the theoretical results are applied to an optimal investment problem with delay in a competitive environment.

title: On SQG Patches with $H^2$ Regularity
authors: Shaoqing Chen, Yongzhong Sun
abstract: In this paper, we study patch solutions of the generalized surface quasi-geostrophic (gSQG) equations, which is an interpolation between the 2D Euler ($β=0$) and the surface quasi-geostrophic (SQG) equations ($β=1$). We establish in the SQG case, the local well-posedness for patches with $H^2$ boundaries, which improves the previous result of $H^{2+s}$, $s>0$ by Gancedo--Nguyen--Patel \cite{Gancedo2022}. Also, in the gSQG case with $0<β<1$, the uniqueness of $H^2$ patch solutions is established. Our proofs are based on the contour dynamics formulation with constant speed, introduced in \cite{Gancedo2008}.

title: Eisenstein Cohomology and Critical Values of Certain \(L\)-Functions: A Root-Theoretic Combinatorial Lemma
authors: Farid Hosseinijafari
abstract: This paper gives a root-theoretic extension of the Harder--Raghuram combinatorial lemma, relating criticality of adjacent $L-$values to degrees in nilradical cohomology, to maximal parabolics $P=MU$ of connected split reductive groups with irreducible, essentially tempered cohomological inducing data. At real places, the paper classifies the maximal parabolics for which the two Kostant degrees in the boundary comparison can agree at a regular shift. For each such parabolic, an admissible shift makes both adjacent arguments critical in every Langlands--Shahidi grade exactly when both Kostant degrees equal $\dim U/2$. The classification recovers the two-block parabolics of type $A$ with even product of block sizes (Harder--Raghuram, proved by Weselmann) and the isotropic-line parabolic of type $D_{2m+1}$ for $m\ge2$ (Bhagwat--Raghuram). The only exceptional cases are $P_1$ and $P_6$ of type $E_6$. In all other cases, roots of $U$ fixed by the longest Levi Weyl element confine simultaneous criticality to a singular wall, generalizing the odd-block obstruction for $\mathrm{GL}_N$. Their number is the difference of the fundamental ranks of $M$ and $G$. When the Kostant degrees differ, as in Harder's $\mathrm{GL}_2$ setting, the paper determines which boundary degrees can still coincide. At a complex place, an admissible shift is simultaneously critical exactly when the two conjugate Levi weights after the shift occur in Kostant degrees summing to $\dim U$. With a common relative center, total degree balance at a regular admissible shift characterizes simultaneous criticality at every archimedean place. For split $E_6$ over $\mathbb Q$, a half-spin family yields Eisenstein cohomology classes in degrees $20$ and $21$, including a degree-$20$ class with nonzero restrictions to both associate boundary face types.

title: Machine learning enables full Bayesian inference for spinning extreme-mass-ratio inspirals
authors: Bo Liang, Minghui Du, Zhenwei Lyu, Hanlin Song, Jiakai Zhang, Weichen Qin, Chia-Jui Chou, Yi Yang, Jingyi Yu, Ziren Luo, Mingming Sun, Peng Xu, Yue-Liang Wu
abstract: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs), stellar-mass compact objects spiralling into massive black holes, promise to measure the masses and spins of the central black holes, reveal the strong-field environment around them and gauge cosmic distances via millihertz gravitational-wave observations. Yet most forecasts for the parameter inference of these systems assume known source parameters, and broad-prior analyses have addressed only simplified versions of the problem. The joint inversion of all 14 parameters of a spinning source from the complete prior has remained unsolved. Here we solve it for the augmented analytic kludge model: generative networks narrow the complete prior and reveal a ring of degenerate spin directions, and the exact detector likelihood determines the posterior. For a simulated one-year LISA-Taiji observation, within one ring sector we obtain, for the first time, a 14-parameter posterior of a spinning EMRI from the complete prior, the most precise yet obtained for such a source from broad priors. The redshifted mass and spin of the massive black hole are determined to two parts in $10^5$, the mass two orders of magnitude beyond any electromagnetic measurement. The compact object's redshifted mass is measured to one part in $10^4$, and its eccentric, retrograde orbit discriminates between capture channels. The 0.8% distance and sub-square-degree localization are sufficient for dark-siren cosmology. Year-long coherent analysis resolves the inspiral driven by radiation reaction itself.

title: Linearization for unbounded perturbations of sublinear growth
authors: Xiao Tang, Jiangqiong Yu
abstract: We investigate global topological linearization with unbounded perturbations of sublinear growth. Under a spectral gap condition and a sufficiently small Lipschitz constant, we show that the displacements of both the conjugacy and its inverse from the identity satisfy the same growth bound as the perturbation. Moreover, the conjugacy is unique within the class of maps whose displacements satisfy this bound. We obtain representations of the displacement in terms of stable and unstable orbit series that converge uniformly on any bounded set and give the inverse conjugacy by using the Banach fixed points theorem in a weighted function space.

title: Your VLM Knows What to Inspect: Semantic Probe-Guided Adaptive Focusing for GUI Grounding
authors: Ruixiao Shi, Fu Feng, Yucheng Xie, Jing Wang, Xin Geng
abstract: GUI grounding requires resolving fine visual details within the context that gives them meaning. Additional views can improve localization, but their value depends on what evidence they expose and how much context they preserve. We explore a capability of vision-language models (VLMs): even when their coordinate predictions are incorrect, they can describe visual evidence worth inspecting. We introduce \textbf{SPARK}, \textit{\textbf{S}emantic \textbf{P}robe-guided \textbf{A}daptive \textbf{R}egion see\textbf{K}ing}, a training-free framework that turns this semantic guidance into targeted visual observations. Exploration probes describe relevant context and distinguishing target details, while verification probes identify evidence needed to assess emerging hypotheses. Their spatial attention guides view placement, contextual responses determine crop extent, and observation history encourages complementary inspection. The resulting predictions are combined through uncertainty-weighted voting. On ScreenSpot-Pro, SPARK improves grounding accuracy over single-view inference by 13.9, 25.2, and 16.1 percentage points with Qwen3-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, and UI-TARS, outperforming all compared test-time methods for each backbone. Consistent gains across four additional benchmarks demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse interfaces and grounding tasks. These results establish semantic probing as an effective mechanism for turning a frozen VLM's understanding of what to inspect into more accurate GUI grounding.

title: A General Framework for E-process Stopping Rules in Best-Arm Identification
authors: Donghyun Park, Seohwa Hwang, Junyong Park
abstract: We propose an e-process stopping rule in the best-arm identification problem. The e-process stopping rule is different from the Chernoff stopping rule by its hypothesis structure on the stopping decision. The major benefit of an e-process stopping rule is the flexibility in stopping rule design and in fact, it recovers previously suggested Chernoff stopping rule on several bandit problems. Moreover, we analyze the asymptotic optimality of the $δ$-PAC algorithm with the decomposition of e-processes. The decomposition separates optimality conditions into three parts; the sampling policy allocation convergence, the efficiency of e-process design, and the bandit problem's inherent stochastic behavior. Subsequently, we prove a sufficient condition for asymptotic optimality in bandit algorithms. For the application of an e-process stopping rule, we derived an asymptotically optimal algorithm for the generalized linear bandit problem.

title: Moiré-Induced Interlayer Electron-Phonon Coupling in Graphene/hBN Superlattices
authors: Dasol Kim, Zhengguang Lu, Tonghang Han, Guorui Chen, Tianyi Han, Jixiang Yang, Bing Cheng, Zhenxian Liu, Christopher Homes, G. L. Carr, Jeong Min Park, Qihang Zhang, Lili Jiang, Hongyuan Li, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Pablo Jarillo-Herrero, Feng Wang, Long Ju
abstract: Electron-phonon coupling (EPC) plays a vital role in the electrical and optical properties of materials, ranging from superconductivity to charge dynamics. In moiré superlattices, out-of-plane vibrations can modulate the moiré potential and enhance interlayer EPC. Here we report the first direct observation of a resonance arising from coupling between moiré electronic excitations and phonons in graphene-based moiré superlattices. Using Fourier-transform infrared photocurrent spectroscopy, we detect the nominally silent hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) out-of-plane optical (ZO) phonon as a pronounced absorption peak. The phonon interferes with moiré flat-band excitations to form a characteristic Fano resonance. Displacement field-dependent measurements confirm that the feature originates from coupling to the moiré electronic continuum rather than simple zone folding. We further observe similar resonances in devices with different graphene layer numbers and twist configurations. This enhanced EPC provides a pathway for understanding and controlling emerging quantum phenomena, such as superconductivity, and engineering novel optoelectronic devices.

title: RESET: One Demonstration, One Verified World, Self-Improved Skills Across Embodiments
authors: Zheng Sun, Zhuo Li, Zhihao Li, Hengyi Sim, Ge Wang, Ziyue Zhu, Mingkai Jia, Fei Chen
abstract: Large language model (LLM) coding agents can iteratively self-improve robot manipulation skills in simulation benchmarks, yet real-world tasks provide neither ground-truth success scorers nor resettable practice environments. Our key observation is that a single real demonstration simultaneously specifies scene geometry, defines the terminal success criterion, and serves as a physical reference trajectory for verifying world fidelity---all decoupled from the source robot's kinematics. We present {RESET}: we reconstruct a contact-rich world and derive a frozen read-only criterion from one demonstration ({R}ebuild); check that world against the demonstration by open-loop replay and silhouette consistency ({E}xamine); evolve modular white-box task graphs and skill code from per-node failure evidence ({S}elf-improve); deploy frozen code on real robots with zero runtime LLM calls ({E}xecute); and share the verified world and criterion with unseen robots without new demonstrations ({T}ransfer). On 8 manipulation tasks, each rebuilt from one real demonstration, RESET achieves 97% average success on unseen layouts in simulation, whereas zero-shot code reaches 27%, per-task fine-tuned pi0.5 policies 31%, and Diffusion Policy 50%; injecting reconstruction defects shows that practice tolerates many reconstruction errors, that geometric errors can still stall or mislead it, and that the check flags most of them while physical randomization covers the rest. Without any target demonstrations, 3 heterogeneous robots acquire the same task skills in the shared world: a robot with similar arms copies 95% of its skill functions unchanged from the source robot, while robots with different arms and hands write their own. In real-robot experiments, the resulting programs run on 4 robots and succeed in 80% of 280 trials.

title: Toward Database-Native Genomics: A Vision for Declarative Genomic Analysis
authors: Dhruv Aron, Danial Saleem, James Christopher Sorenson, Xiangyao Yu
abstract: In recent years, numerous advancements in relational database management systems (RDBMS), including cloud-native and GPU-native paradigms, have resulted in highly competitive RDBMS performance for analytical workloads. At the same time, the field of genomics has evolved into a data-intensive domain owing to the advent of next-generation sequencing; however, current genomic analysis workflows are often file-based, fragmented, and reliant on disparate tools, limiting their expressiveness, usability, performance, and scalability. This work argues for an incremental adoption of RDBMS and declarative SQL querying in genomic analysis, particularly tertiary analysis. By translating common tasks from widely-used tools like SAMtools and BEDtools into SQL queries executed in DuckDB, we demonstrate that off-the-shelf RDBMS can match or exceed the performance of existing tools while offering significant improvements in expressiveness and usability. We identify current limitations and propose practical paths forward, aiming to position relational databases as a foundational platform for modern bioinformatics workflows.

title: Cheap Memory Costs Future Compute: Co-Designing Persistent KV and GPU Execution for Efficient Streaming Video Diffusion
authors: Jian Yang, Zhizhuo Kou, Qiyuan Zhu, Han Chen, Sirui Han, Yike Guo
abstract: Block-causal video diffusion generates long videos block by block, conditioned on a persistent key-value (KV) cache. After each block is denoised, an extra noise-free ($t=0$) forward pass writes its clean KV into the cache; once distillation and speculative early exit make denoising cheap, this clean KV update dominates the runtime. Reusing stale KV shortens the update, but stale memory corrupts the conditioning of later blocks and inflates their denoising steps, so the saved compute reappears downstream. We present SAMR (Step-Aware Memory Reconstruction), a training-free method for frozen causal video DiTs that refreshes only part of the cache and reconstructs the rest without DiT forwards. Our key observation is that, once rotary position phases are removed, motion-aligned historical KV and the in-flight KV a token holds at its exit step are complementary estimates of its clean KV. SAMR debiases in-flight KV with offline-calibrated per-head affine maps in Pre-RoPE space, fuses the two estimates, and reserves true $t=0$ refreshes for tokens flagged by an attention-readout error proxy, all executed by tile-aligned, synchronization-free Triton kernels. On 48-second LongLive-1.3B videos, SAMR reduces DiT latency by 20.9% and principal FLOPs by 30.7% relative to dense KV updates, lowers downstream denoising steps, and improves final-quarter PSNR over token reuse by 1.61 dB (1.14 dB on held-out VidProM-16). The reconstruction also transfers to frozen Self-Forcing-DMD-1.3B: zero-shot, it reduces reuse-induced step inflation ($2.47 \to 2.30$ steps/token) and improves late PSNR by $+0.33$ dB, and a one-time training-free calibration recovers the diagnostic score that zero-shot transfer lowers ($89.62 \to 91.10$).

title: Needlepoints in Quasi-Normed Orlicz Spaces and a Question of Kalton and Peck
authors: Dong Ji, Yunan Cui
abstract: We prove that the approachable points and the needlepoints coincide in every quasi-normed Orlicz function space on the probability interval. Their common set is either $\{0\}$ or $E_Φ$. The proof gives a characterization by finite probability laws and also applies to Orlicz function spaces with the modular topology, without assuming $Δ_2$. We then construct a separable real quasi-Banach space whose approachable points form a line and whose only needlepoint is zero. Every compact convex subset of this space is relatively locally convex. The construction gives a negative answer to the question of Kalton and Peck for general quasi-Banach spaces.

title: Infinite lower triangular matrices that are similar to their inverses but are not products of two involutions
authors: Pham The Nhan
abstract: Let $F$ be a field, and let $\GL_{\cf}(F)$ be the group of invertible column-finite matrices over $F$ indexed by $\bbN\times\bbN$. Denote by $\LT(F)$ (resp.\ $\UT(F)$) the subgroup consisting of lower (resp.\ upper) triangular matrices whose diagonal entries are equal to $1$. Every matrix in $\UT(F)$ is a product of two involutions. We show that, if $F$ has at least four elements, then $\LT(F)$ contains a matrix which is conjugate to its inverse by an invertible lower triangular matrix, but is not a product of two involutions in $\GL_{\cf}(F)$. The matrices can be chosen to be $4$-periodic. This gives a negative answer to a conjecture of de Seguins Pazzis.

title: Multi Agent Reinforcement Learning enhanced Federated Learning for Predicting Remaining Useful Lifetime
authors: Rajarshi Chattopadhyay, Chen-Khong Tham
abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is central to Prognostics and Health Management (PHM). The growth of industrial IoT has unlocked large multivariate sensor streams and enabled deep models - especially Transformers - for long-horizon sequence learning. However, transformers are parameter-heavy and data-hungry, while operational datasets are often siloed and privacy-sensitive. Federated Learning (FL) addresses this by training across clients without raw data sharing, but in practice many clients connect over lossy wireless links where UDP is preferred for low latency, making model exchange vulnerable to packet drops. We present a cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework that adapts FL to lossy channels by selecting per-client layer subsets to transmit and capping retransmissions. This framework is trained with QMIX value-function factorization for scalability. We instantiate the approach with a Graph Convolution Position-Aware Transformer (GCPATr) for RUL forecasting. On the CMAPSS dataset, our MARL-enhanced FL (RL-FL) consistently improves mean square error over standard FL, with the largest gains at high packet loss (e.g., up to 18% improvement on FD003 at 50% loss). These results show that MARL is an effective countermeasure to wireless degradation in FL-based RUL prediction.

title: VidForce: Predicting Force-Aware Articulation by Observing Humans
authors: Rafay Mohiuddin, Jiaqi Chen, Marc Pollefeys, Hermann Blum
abstract: People can anticipate how an object moves and the effort an interaction may require by watching others. How can embodied agents acquire this understanding from video? Force measurements provide direct sensory supervision, but require specialized equipment and remain limited in quantity. We introduce VidForce, which estimates an interaction trajectory together with a force profile from a third-person RGB video; 2D contact clicks and textual object-action prompts are optional. Our approach makes limited instrumented measurements useful for interpreting human interactions through learned physical prototypes as a prior. The prototypes share learned force levels and temporal profiles across interactions of comparable effort, with visual and semantic cues determining their contribution to each observation. Geometric and vision-language features adapt this prior to the observed interaction, while a joint conditional flow refines an initial tracked trajectory together with the force profile. Paired human and instrumented-gripper recordings provide measured force references for supervising human video, and a separately trained torque model demonstrates that the formulation extends to other sensory quantities. We evaluate trajectory recovery and force estimation through baseline comparisons and controlled ablations on held-out interactions from the Hoi! dataset. On this evaluation subset, VidForce achieves 6.6 cm ATE, peak-force MAE and RMSE of 4.81 N and 5.92 N, respectively, and force-profile RMSE of 5.52 N. On real-world videos, VidForce infers motion and force reliably and consistently despite the variability in human execution. We further deploy VidForce on a Spot robot, where trajectories and force profiles estimated from human demonstrations drive real-world articulated-object manipulation, and report success rates across repeated trials. Project page: https://rafaymhddn.github.io/vidforce

title: Anomalous front propagation in many-body quantum transport with memory-dependent resetting
authors: Gabriele de Mauro, Manas Kulkarni, Satya N. Majumdar
abstract: We introduce an exactly solvable framework for non-Markovian quantum many-body dynamics based on stochastic resetting with memory. Applicable to arbitrary time-independent Hamiltonians, including interacting systems, our framework provides an exact representation of the dynamics with memory in terms of the corresponding reset-free evolution, which can be accessed either analytically or numerically. We demonstrate the power of this approach by studying domain-wall melting in a one-dimensional chain of noninteracting fermions, obtaining exact analytical results for the density profile, the local structure of the front edge, the extreme-value statistics of the rightmost fermion, and the integrated current. Remarkably, memory transforms ballistic transport into logarithmically slow propagation without arresting spreading. While the macroscopic density profile retains its original scaling function, the front edge broadens as $\sqrt{\ln t}$ rather than $t^{1/3}$ at late times and develops a qualitatively different edge structure. Furthermore, the extreme-value statistics change from Tracy--Widom to Gaussian, while both the mean and variance of the integrated current grow logarithmically in time. Our predictions are in excellent agreement with numerical simulations. These results reveal how memory can fundamentally alter quantum many-body transport and its fluctuations.

title: Exact local queries for pseudo-marginal Markov chains
authors: Zihan Xu
abstract: Local queries of a Markov chain can depend on past updates outside the queried components. For pseudo-marginal chains with Gaussian graph priors, we construct decision certificates from finite historical parameter ranges to settle updates before all neighbouring records are resolved. Under shared random inputs and exact arithmetic, the executor recovers the reference parameters, auxiliary variables and likelihood estimates for any prespecified finite query sequence. We bound conditional expected work, including likelihood evaluation, historical range construction and execution management. On specified path and grid families, we fix per-node history lengths and all other parameters in the work bounds. As graph size grows, expected incremental work stays bounded for certificate execution and grows linearly for the specified cached pointwise evaluator answering the same query. In controlled experiments, certificate execution is faster than pointwise and parallel Picard execution for sparse queries, whereas Picard is faster than certificate execution for full queries. We apply the method to positron emission tomography and Gaussian process classification of Landmine data. For a fixed numerical tomography posterior, certificate execution completes all queries of regional mean distribution volume within budget, while full execution completes none from the same initial cache. In Landmine, posterior summaries of the difference in log length scales between two sites agree across pseudo-marginal and ancillary augmentation samplers within estimated Monte Carlo uncertainty. Certificate execution resolves almost every scheduled update over the full query sequence.

title: LoomKV: Lossless KV Cache Compression from GPU Memory to SSD for LLM Serving
authors: Wentao Zhu, Ziao Sheng, Peng Deng, Huiqi Hu, Xuan Zhou, Xing Wei, Zhuang Wang
abstract: Large language model (LLM) serving engines offload the key/value (KV) cache from GPU memory to host DRAM and SSD so multi-turn and agent requests can reuse prompt prefixes. Capacity then limits service at two levels: external tiers govern prefix reuse before eviction, while the GPU KV pool bounds concurrent long requests, and lossy compression alters KV values and outputs. LoomKV brings lossless KV compression to both external tiers (tier mode) and the GPU pool (pool mode) on an unmodified engine. Using a calibrated per-head two-level 3-bit code over BF16 high bytes (sign and upper seven exponent bits), LoomKV stores BF16 KV at 0.71 of its raw size across nine models and FP8 KV at 0.85-0.87. In tier mode, TileStream writes exact-length records with length readback off the load path, leaving tier storage, eviction, and prefetch unchanged, and decompresses fetched records straight into scattered GPU pages. In pool mode, FragPack packs variable-length records into smaller shared-budget GPU pages read in place by a fused decode-attention kernel faster than FlashAttention-3 on BF16. Built with LMCache and vLLM, LoomKV makes compressed tiers act as 1.4x larger raw tiers on AgentX: across LMCache's LRU cliff, tier mode delivers 2.7-3.6x raw's goodput and 1.9-3.1x lower mean time-to-first-token (TTFT), shifts the cliff identically under other simulated replacement policies, and cuts repeated-prompt TTFT up to 1.7x via SSD-to-DRAM promotion. When tiers hold the working set, pool mode fits 1.31-1.34x as many GPU tokens, admitting 12 long requests with roughly raw's queue and goodput at 8. On an AI IDE trace where both tiers and the GPU pool are constrained, tier and pool modes raise goodput by 1.24x and 1.59x. Where raw capacity suffices, compression costs at most 2.2% throughput; tier mode is bit-exact with raw tiers, and pool mode matches FlashAttention-3's numerical accuracy.

title: ShellBench: What Matters More for AI Agents, Models, or Harness for Everyday Tasks
authors: Vincent Koc, Aditya Washikar, Rishab Naveen Venkataraman, Onur Solmaz, Zhentong Fan, Xinyang Han, Toby Vincent John, Hao Li, Achyut Mukund, Biresh Chandra Biswas, Eshan Shukla, Louis Pan, Ivan Kudryavtsev, Patthigulla Sai Surendra, Krish Oberoi, Ayaan Zaidi, Hema Veeradhi, Taylor Agarwal, Erik Erlandson, Agustin Rivera, Jacob Tomlinson, Louka Ewington-Pitsos
abstract: The use of AI agents among the general public has been increasing exponentially throughout 2026, though it is often hard for users to determine which configuration is most effective for their personal use. To help provide clarity here we introduce ShellBench, 100 day-to-day tasks based on more than 10 million user requests, each set in a realistic workspace with messy files and competing data sources, and graded for both correctness and safety. We evaluate 12 models across 5 agent harnesses at 3 reasoning levels for a total of 53,100 rollouts, 20% of which are on tasks designated for public release. We find that model choice impacts performance more than harness choice, but the three leading models differ by only 1.1 percentage points. GPT-6.1 Sol passed 61.4% of attempts at about one-sixth of GPT-6 Astra's estimated token cost per attempt, while GPT-6 Astra led at 62.5%. We also found that harness choice had little effect on either performance or safety with all harnesses scoring between 42.9 (Claude Code) and 45.2 (OpenClaw) for pass@1.

title: PHM-ensemble: Scalable and Stable Probabilistic Multiresolution Clustering via Ensemble Density Estimation
authors: Ali Turfah, Xiaoquan Wen
abstract: Clustering is a foundational tool for exploratory data analysis across the sciences. We argue that clustering methods should be evaluated along four dimensions: fidelity to the data's underlying structure, interpretability of the recovered groups, stability under data perturbations and algorithmic randomness, and scalability to modern scientific datasets. Yet existing methods rarely satisfy all four criteria. To address this gap, we introduce PHM-ensemble, a general probabilistic framework for multiresolution clustering that estimates the underlying data density by pooling mixture models from an ensemble of fits and subsequently constructs a clustering hierarchy through hierarchical merging of the mixture components. On simulated datasets and the MNIST benchmark, PHM-ensemble matches or outperforms widely used clustering algorithms in agreement with ground truth, produces more stable results across runs, and reveals complex underlying structures. Applied to 1.82 million peripheral blood cells from the Human Immune Health Atlas, PHM-ensemble achieves higher agreement with expert-curated major cell-type annotations than the Leiden clustering used in the original study (adjusted Rand index 0.965 versus 0.789), while requiring only half the computing time. Beyond identifying major immune lineages, it reveals biologically coherent relationships among cell types and resolves finer structure within individual lineages, uncovering subtypes and cellular states consistent with known biology.

title: Quantum kernels on breast data: concentration, surrogates, and two ways an advantage gets manufactured
authors: Rana Saad, Achraf Toufah, Moulay Youssef El Hafidi
abstract: Quantum-kernel advantage claims on breast data are usually a single number: one quantum arm, one comparator, one test split. We asked what that number measures once the full comparator set and selection history are visible. We report three active benchmarks, all exact classical statevector simulations of 8-qubit fidelity kernels with no quantum component in the inference path: a sample-efficiency sweep on Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer at ten training-set sizes; raw-versus-processed arms on 1,200 M-SYNTH simulated mammograms with a matched closed-form dequantisation surrogate, five classical methods at the same input and eleven kernel families; and a 30-seed selection-inflation measurement on BreastMNIST. A CMMD D1 clinical arm is withdrawn as a result arm because its frozen splits leak the label through patient serial order, a defect reported in a separate study; it is retained only as a worked example. All three active arms are negative. On M-SYNTH raw an apparent +0.1736 (p = 5.2e-06) against a tuned RBF-SVM falls to +0.0019 (p = 0.937) against a random forest at the same input, and a Laplacian kernel wins on validation. On WDBC, with model selection confined to training data, the quantum kernel is below the selected classical arm at every training-set size, with 2 of 200 paired subsamples ahead. Best-of-30 seed selection adds +0.0210 on BreastMNIST. One result does not fit: at bandwidth 2pi the matched closed-form Gaussian surrogate failed to reproduce the M-SYNTH raw kernel (0.5410 against 0.7045, p = 6.3e-06). Comparator choice and selection each produce effects larger than any quantum-classical difference we measured; we give a reporting standard that removes both.

title: Self-Sensing Compliant Anthropomorphic Hand for Speed-Dictated Shared Force Control in Teleoperation
authors: Huijiang Wang, Yu Zhang, Rui Chen, Tristan Bonato, Jaemin Eom, Kai Junge, Cheng Pan, Benhui Dai, Yue Xie, Josie Hughes
abstract: In vision-based teleoperation of robotic hands, the operator receives no haptic feedback and therefore struggles to regulate the grasp force, while adding tactile sensors to the fingers increases wiring, cost and integration complexity. Compliant hands offer an alternative, as their mechanical compliance, usually treated only as a passive property for safe and adaptive grasping, can also serve as a source of information. Here, we show that the elastic transmission of a compliant, tendon-driven anthropomorphic hand can itself act as the sensor for shared-control telemanipulation. Series springs in the tendon routing are read by potentiometers in a forearm-mounted motor box, from which the hand estimates its joint states and finger forces without any external sensors. Building on this self-sensing, we develop a contact-aware shared-control framework for VR-based teleoperation. The robot hand is controlled through a mapping from the operator's hand kinematics until a contact is detected proprioceptively. Control then switches to a finger-level force controller whose set point is determined by the operator's grasping speed, and control authority can be allocated to individual fingers. Experiments validate the system's force estimation and increased grasp success rate compared with direct teleoperation for fragile and heavy objects. These results show that compliance can serve not only for passive adaptation but also as an intrinsic sensing resource for physical human-robot collaboration.

title: Statistical Process Monitoring of Functional Linear Models
authors: Davide Forcina, Antonio Lepore, Kamran Paynabar
abstract: Monitoring the stability over time of the relationship between a functional response and multiple functional covariates is important in many industrial applications, either because the relationship itself is the quality characteristic of interest or because it underpins a predictive model whose validity must be verified as the process evolves. Existing methods either assume the model estimated in Phase I to be stable and monitor the resulting residuals, or re-estimate its coefficients at each sampling stage, which requires several observations to be available at a time. In this article, we propose the regression coefficient function (RCF) control chart to monitor functional linear models (FLMs) in which, at each sampling stage, an individual observation of the functional response and an arbitrary number of functional covariates become available. The proposed method employs an exponentially weighted moving loss to sequentially update estimates of the regression coefficient functions and the intercept function, which are monitored through Hotelling's $T^2$ and squared prediction error (SPE) control charts. A post-signal diagnostic procedure is also provided to support the identification of the source of the detected change. A Monte Carlo simulation study demonstrates that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods, particularly against small and persistent shifts, and a case study on monitoring the relationship between the air/fuel ratio and engine state variables in an automotive after-treatment system illustrates its practical applicability.

title: Integrated lasing and dual-band gain in neodymium-implanted silicon nitride
authors: Jan de Haan, Arturo Fernández Gamez, Nina Zdravković, Kevin Kwock, Ulrich Kentsch, Rene Heller, Alberto Curto, Bart Kuyken, Kasper Van Gasse
abstract: Lasers at wavelengths near 1 micrometer are used in quantum technologies, precision metrology, and sensing. Rare-earth gain at these wavelengths in photonic integrated circuits can reduce the size and enable the scalable fabrication of these lasers. We fabricate neodymium-based integrated waveguide amplifiers and a ring laser using neodymium-implanted LPCVD silicon nitride. The photonic integrated circuits were fabricated on a 200 mm commercial wafer platform, and individual dies were implanted with neodymium ions. We show that the amplifiers provide gain in two bands around wavelengths of 920 nm and 1100 nm, and we show lasing in a ring resonator. This demonstrates that neodymium-implanted LPCVD silicon nitride is a suitable gain material for integrated lasers.

title: Entanglement Asymmetry and the Quantum Mpemba Effect in Inhomogeneous Quenches
authors: Maëlle Olivier, Filiberto Ares, Pasquale Calabrese
abstract: Entanglement asymmetry is a powerful probe of symmetry breaking and its dynamical restoration following quantum quenches. While extensively studied for homogeneous initial states, its evolution from inhomogeneous initial configurations remains largely unexplored. We investigate a spin-$1/2$ XX chain whose two halves are initially prepared in tilted ferromagnetic states with different tilt angles. Combining generalized hydrodynamics (GHD) and the quasiparticle picture with exact fermionic correlation-matrix calculations, we study the dynamics of entanglement asymmetry. We find good agreement between the two approaches for generic initial configurations and observe the quantum Mpemba effect, whereby states with stronger initial symmetry breaking can restore the symmetry faster. This effect now depends on the subsystem position: while the homogeneous behavior is recovered when the subsystem lies entirely within one of the initially tilted halves, the entanglement-asymmetry curves for subsystems straddling the interface can exhibit multiple crossings or no crossings at all. A notable exception occurs for subsystems entirely within an initially non-tilted half. In this case, GHD predicts vanishing asymmetry, but the exact dynamics generates a small, nonzero asymmetry that can develop a plateau before decaying toward zero. This feature reveals contributions beyond the leading-order hydrodynamic description.

title: An exponential-rate consensus-based algorithms for estimation from relative measurements: implementation and performance analysis
authors: Ruggero Carli, Andrea Carron, Luca Schenato, Marco Todescato
abstract: In this work we address the problem of optimal estimating the position of each agent in a network from relative noisy vectorial distances with its neighbors. Although the problem can be cast as a standard least-squares problem, the main challenge is to devise scalable algorithms that allow each agent to estimate its own position by means of only local communication and bounded complexity, independently of the network size and topology. We first propose a synchronous consensus-based algorithm that is guaranteed to have exponentially convergence rate to the optimal centralized least-squares solution. We then extend this algorithm to more realistic asynchronous implementations via the use of local memory variables. We show that exponential convergence is still guaranteed under both uniform persistent communication and randomized persistent communication protocols. We finally complement the analytical results with some numerical simulations.

title: Better-than-3 Approximation for 2ECSS Using the Primal-Dual Method
authors: Ana Cezara Danciu, Sharat Ibrahimpur
abstract: In the $2$-edge-connected spanning subgraph problem (2ECSS), we are given an undirected multigraph whose edges have nonnegative costs, and the goal is to find a $2$-edge-connected spanning subgraph with minimum total cost. Two distinct approaches yield $2$-approximation algorithms: a reduction to the minimum-cost rooted $2$-arborescence problem and iterative rounding. Despite significant efforts, the best known approximation ratio using the primal-dual method has remained at $3$. Our main result in this work is a primal-dual algorithm for 2ECSS that achieves an approximation ratio of $\sqrt{3}+1 (\leq 2.74)$. The algorithm runs in a single phase and the approximation guarantee is relative to the natural linear relaxation, which requires the sum of the edge variables across every cut to be at least $2$. The algorithm follows the standard template of growing dual variables corresponding to minimal violated sets, albeit at non-uniform rates, until the dual constraint for an edge becomes tight, at which point the edge is temporarily purchased. Once feasibility is attained, redundant edges are dropped in the reverse order in which they were purchased. Our choice of dual growth rates is inspired by the single-phase $3$-approximation algorithm of Beyer, Chimani, and Spoerhase (COCOON 2020). As in their work, our algorithm maintains a forest of purchased edges by repeatedly contracting $2$-edge-connected subgraphs, and dual variables corresponding to leaves and isolated vertices of this forest are grown at a rate of $1$. Our main modification is to additionally grow dual variables corresponding to nontrivial connected components at rate $(\sqrt{3}-1)/2 \approx 0.37$, when the forest is disconnected.

title: Whistler instability driven by electron trapping in magnetic dips
authors: Ida Svenningsson, István Pusztai, Konrad Steinvall, Tünde Fülöp
abstract: Using fully kinetic particle-in-cell simulations, we show how free energy released by an ion-scale instability reaches electron scales through its effect on the electron distribution. An initial ion temperature anisotropy drives partly compressional ion cyclotron waves, which form magnetic dips. Electrons trapped in these dips develop an enhanced temperature anisotropy and butterfly-shaped distributions, similar to those observed by spacecraft in the Earth's magnetosheath. By tracking the energy transfer in velocity space, we show that the gradients created by trapping drive whistler waves through cyclotron resonance. The whistlers in turn scatter the electrons in pitch angle, flattening velocity-space gradients and heating the electrons along the magnetic field. As a result, the electron anisotropy drops to about half of the double-adiabatic prediction once the whistler power peaks. Our results show that it is the shape of the electron distribution in magnetic dips, rather than its temperature anisotropy alone, that drives the whistlers.

title: From Fermions to Vortices: Microscopic Simulations of Phase Ordering in a d-Wave Superconductor
authors: Ali Rayat, Gia-Wei Chern
abstract: Describing bath-induced superconducting phase ordering directly from a microscopic fermionic Hamiltonian remains a formidable challenge. Here we develop a microscopic framework for this problem using the recently introduced adiabatic variational principle (AVP) and demonstrate its application to a two-dimensional $d$-wave superconductor. The central construction maps evolving, spatially inhomogeneous bond-pairing fields onto constrained Bogoliubov-de Gennes states, with the associated Lagrange multipliers determining the thermodynamic driving forces. This enables dissipative evolution of the superconducting order while retaining its microscopic electronic structure, without assuming a phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau free-energy functional. Starting from disordered pairing configurations, we resolve the emergence of phase coherence through vortex-antivortex annihilation and the accompanying evolution of local electronic spectra. Vortex decay and dynamical scaling recover the characteristic kinetics of two-dimensional phase ordering, providing a nontrivial benchmark of the framework. The solver-independent AVP formulation opens a route to microscopic studies of dissipative ordering and metastability in superconductors with intertwined stripe and pair-density-wave orders.

title: Compositional Reachset-Conformant Modeling for Managing Uncertainty in the Development of Cyber-Physical Systems
authors: Laura Lützow, Francesco Pio Urbano, Tobias Düser, Matthias Althoff
abstract: The development of cyber-physical systems (CPS) proceeds through iterative design revisions, and compliance with safety requirements must be re-established after every revision, typically based on a system model. Conventional models, however, predict only the most likely behavior, leading to model-plant mismatch that often surfaces only during late-stage testing, when redesign is most expensive. This article presents reachset-conformant modeling as a framework for managing uncertainty throughout the development process: instead of a single trajectory, a reachset-conformant model predicts a set of behaviors, calibrated from data to conservatively enclose the true system behavior with a statistical guarantee. Safety properties established on the model therefore transfer to the realized system. Beyond a practical introduction to reachset-conformant identification and its benefits for CPS development, our main theoretical contribution is a closure result: reachset conformance is preserved under serial composition, parallel composition, and feedback interconnection, and hence under any architecture assembled from these primitives. Subsystem models identified independently from local measurements can thus be substituted into the system architecture, and the interconnected model inherits a coverage guarantee from the subsystem guarantees. We complement this result with update strategies that adapt the uncertainty sets after design changes without restarting the identification workflow. Experiments on an automotive brake-system test bench demonstrate that a) a single model covers all operating conditions and hardware variants, b) late-stage modifications are absorbed by uncertainty set updates, c) a black-box hydraulic unit is conservatively abstracted from input-output data alone, and d) independently identified subsystem models form a conformant model by construction.

title: Elimination Methods for Computing Invariant Algebraic Surfaces and Hopf Bifurcations
authors: Changbo Chen, Bo Huang, Valery Romanovski, Linpeng Wang
abstract: This paper presents efficient algorithmic methods for computing invariant algebraic surfaces and Hopf bifurcations in parametric polynomial differential systems. For invariant algebraic surfaces of bounded degree, we establish two complementary elimination frameworks: combining Gröbner bases with saturation and prime decomposition yields the Zariski closure of the parameter existence locus (necessary conditions), whereas triangular decomposition into strong regular systems recovers the exact pointwise constructible locus (necessary and sufficient conditions) via the projection property. We further present a hybrid approach for identifying such surfaces by integrating prime decomposition with branch-wise triangular solving, thereby efficiently deriving necessary and sufficient conditions with enhanced computational flexibility and rectifying subtle classification errors in a class of Liénard systems. For Hopf bifurcations, extending prior work on necessary conditions [SIAM J. Numer. Anal. 34 (1997)] and sufficient conditions [J. Math. Anal. Appl. 182 (1994); J. Symbolic Comput. 30 (2000)], we establish a complete algebraic characterization via two equivalent formulations: one using Hurwitz determinants and subresultant sequences, and another derived from the greatest common divisor (GCD) of the real and imaginary parts of the characteristic polynomial. From the GCD formulation, we obtain a novel and, for the first time, complete semi-algebraic description of the transversality condition, yielding a decision procedure via triangular decomposition of semi-algebraic systems and heuristic real quantifier elimination. Our approach resolves cases beyond the reach of state-of-the-art polynomial-based methods, and experimental results confirm the feasibility and efficiency of our frameworks.

title: TESS discovers an eclipse of the Be star V1294 Aql (= HD 184279) by its not-so-small, low-mass companion
authors: J. Labadie-Bartz, D. Baade, Th. Rivinius, R. Klement
abstract: In a single sector of observations with the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS), an eclipse-like event occurred in the Be star V1294 Aql. The reality of the eclipse is corroborated by $UBV$ photometry from the Hvar observatory. The event occurred at phase 17.97 of the linear ephemeris by Harmanec et al. (2022) for the upper conjunction of this SB1 binary (P$_{\rm orb}$ = 192.9 d). Therefore, we conclude that the Be star was eclipsed by its companion. With this elimination of the uncertainty of the orbital inclination, the mass of the secondary is 0.99 to 1.17 M$_\odot$ for masses of the primary from 14 to 18 M$_{\odot}$. The depth of the eclipse of $\sim$6.0% (0.06 mag) is incompatible with a white-dwarf (WD) nature of the companion. At the implied radius of $\sim$25% of that of the B0.5 primary, the secondary is not a bona-fide sdO/sdB star, either, but it could be still in its contraction phase. The increasing number of such stars may lend support to model calculations according to which the timescale of the contraction can be not thermal but instead is governed by the much slower removal of a residual H-rich envelope. It is also possible the companion is on the pre-main sequence in which case the two stars have not yet interacted. Two new interferometric observations were obtained near orbital quadrature but the secondary star was not detected, nor was it detected in high-resolution high-S/N echelle spectra.

title: Trotterized hybrid qubit-boson simulation of the Jaynes-Cummings-Hubbard model
authors: Nabaraj Khatri, Dilip Ojha, Rajib Tripathi, Kismat K. C, Ashish Khanal
abstract: The Jaynes-Cummings-Hubbard (JCH) model describes the interaction of light and matter in coupled optical cavities and provides a framework for studying their quantum dynamics. In this work, we design a Trotterized quantum circuit to investigate the real-time dynamics of the JCH model using Bosonic Qiskit and a Matrix Product State (MPS) backend. We simulate single-polariton transport and benchmark site occupations against exact diagonalization results. We then extend the simulations to the two-excitation sector under a hard-core photon constraint, examining excitation transport and symmetry properties. Finally, we study the dependence of bipartite entanglement entropy on the inter-cavity photon-hopping strength. The results illustrate how hybrid qubit-boson circuits, simulated with matrix product states, can be used to study light-matter lattice dynamics. This work provides a numerical benchmark for extending hybrid simulation approaches to more complex interacting and open light-matter systems.

title: Shared information governs multi-view planted matching
authors: Ruiqi Wang, Jingtong Hu
abstract: We study when the rows of $K$ shuffled views of the same $n$ objects can be matched, where each object is observed once in every view through a Gaussian feature vector with known covariance. For every fixed $K$, all views can be matched up to $o(n)$ errors if the shared information $J$ of one object's $K$ observations exceeds $(1+ε)\log n$, and not if it is below $(1-ε)\log n$; this can hold although no two views can be matched on their own. Below the threshold, two views can still be matched if some set of views containing both has shared information above $\log n$; otherwise every estimator, even one that reads all views, has vanishing overlap between them. Matching every row is governed by the weakest bipartition of the views: with weak correlations the threshold is $2\log n$ for the mutual information across it. For a weak common signal observed through independent noise, the two thresholds are $4/K$ and $4/(K-1)$ in units of $\sum_\ellρ_\ell^2/\log n$, which answers a question of Wee, Yang, Fan and Mao. Beyond weak correlations the bipartition condition is not sufficient: rare subpopulations impose a Rényi condition for every partition into at least three blocks. We conjecture that the two conditions together characterize exact recovery for Gaussian laws, and prove this for three views with equal correlations and in several further cases, in part with computer assistance. With equal correlations, layered screening attains $4/K$ for $K=3,4$ in $O(Kn^2d)$ operations, and for general laws a recursive decoder attains $J$. The almost-exact thresholds extend to known product laws and to objects observed in random subsets of the views.

title: Global regularities for the Dirichlet problem of Monge-Ampère type equations
authors: Feida Jiang, Jiakun Liu, Jian Lu, Chuanlong Sun
abstract: We establish global a priori $W^{2,p}$ and $C^{2,α}$ estimates for elliptic solutions of the Dirichlet problem for cost-generated Monge-Ampère type equations under the weak Ma-Trudinger-Wang condition A3w, assuming continuous and Hölder continuous right-hand sides, respectively.

title: Lazy Agents Answer Against Their Own Beliefs: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs Teaches Them to Act on What They Believe
authors: Richmond Sin Jing Xuan, Peilin Feng, Wenbin Wang, Soujanya Poria
abstract: AI agents working on long tasks often commit to an answer before they have enough evidence, a behavior called laziness. In our evaluations, they frequently commit even while their stated belief still names several possible answers. An outcome reward at the end of the episode scores only the final answer, so it cannot teach the agent when to commit, because a lucky guess receives the same reward as an answer backed by evidence. During training, however, the simulator can compute the exact posterior over the answer at every step and tell whether the evidence is already enough. We propose Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs (RLVB), which rewards the agent for taking further steps while this posterior still allows several answers and for committing once the evidence is sufficient. The reward needs no judge, critic or reward model, and it never reads the belief line the agent writes before each action. We also introduce Pro Worlds, a benchmark of visual puzzles where the agent views a large world through a small window. We evaluate three vision-language models on three benchmarks, two of which are never seen in training. RLVB improves the base model in all nine settings, by 17.1% on average. Under the outcome reward, GRPO and PPO fall below the base model on average. RLVB also outperforms PPO with a process reward from an LLM judge by 9.3% on average while using 1.6 times fewer GPU-hours. The trained agent answers with sufficient evidence in 51%, 12% and 74% of the episodes on the three benchmarks, against 8%, 0.4% and 36% for the base model. Its accuracy gain therefore comes from answering more often at high levels of evidence. The belief line shows how the agent reaches this evidence: it acts on its own belief. It commits at only 0.1 to 2.2% of the turns at which the evidence is insufficient and its line still names several answers, against 3 to 68% for the base model.

title: Adaptive Electromagnetic Transient-level Digital Twins for Data Centers via In-Context Learning with LLMs
authors: Amit Jena, Bin Wang, Aoxia Chen, Brad Chadwell, Billy Yancey, Le Xie
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) workloads has significantly increased data center (DC) power demand. Frequent operational and configurational changes, such as load surges caused by dynamic workload allocation, can induce electromagnetic transients (EMTs) whose accurate prediction is critical for reliable DC operation and maintenance. Although high-fidelity EMT solvers are widely adopted for transient analysis, their computational cost limits large-scale and multi-scenario studies. Digital twins address this computational bottleneck by emulating the behavior of a physical system and enabling fast prediction in place of expensive high-fidelity simulation. However,data-driven digital twins are non-adaptive and fail to generalize once the DC configuration changes. To address this limitation, this paper proposes an adaptive EMT-level digital twin for DCs based on in-context learning (ICL) with large language models (LLMs). We formulate the EMT prediction task as a system identification problem under parametric uncertainty and develop a GPT-2-based framework that adapts to unseen DC configurations at inference time from a small set of EMT trajectory samples, without model retraining. The proposed framework is validated on three representative EMT scenarios and benchmarked against three baseline non-adaptive twins. Results demonstrate superior prediction accuracy, improved adaptability to unseen operating conditions, and substantial computational speedups compared to high-fidelity EMT simulation.

title: Semi-local Zariski-van Kampen theorems
authors: Helmut A. Hamm
abstract: Zariski-van Kampen theorems are meant to constitute a complement to Lefschetz-Zariski theorems which, in turn, generalize the classical Lefschetz theorem on hyperplane sections to quasi-projective varieties or to the corresponding local case. Semi-local Zariski-van Kampen theorems are developed here as a tool which is useful both in the local and in the global case.

title: A short proof of Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture
authors: Romain Bourneuf, Pierre Charbit, Samuel Coulomb, Stéphan Thomassé
abstract: We give a short alternative proof of Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture, recently proved by OpenAI. Our proof combines their reduction with a different argument showing that every nontrivial oriented graph $G$ contains a nonempty set $X$ such that $X^+\ne V(G)$ and $|(X^+)^+\setminus X^+|\geq|X^+\setminus X|$, where $X^+=N_G^+[X]$.

title: AI, Bias, and Inclusion: A Two-Phase Mixed-Methods Study of Gender Bias, Awareness, and Trust in Artificial Intelligence
authors: MD Junayed Talukdar, Khosro Salmani
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are widespread across fields such as healthcare, finance, employment, and criminal justice, with a substantial impact on the lives of individuals and society. However, it has been established that AI systems perpetuate existing social inequalities, particularly through biases that are not easily discernible. Such biases are embedded in the technical and social structures of artificial intelligence systems, making them difficult to detect. These biases challenge the concept of Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion (EDI), which recognizes diversity as the acknowledgment of individual differences, equity as fairness and equal access, and inclusion as the value placed on all participants. This study argues that fairness in artificial intelligence systems cannot be achieved by focusing solely on their technical aspects, necessitating a holistic approach. This study employs a two-phase mixed-methods design. Phase 1 applies computational content analysis to 360 occupational narratives generated by ChatGPT across four countries (Canada, Germany, India, and Bangladesh) using gender-neutral prompts to examine whether professions are predominantly associated with one gender and whether these patterns remain consistent across regions. Phase 2 examines the extent to which students recognize potential bias in AI, their trust in AI for consequential decision-making, and how these perceptions relate to themes in EDI and AI ethics scholarship. By combining output-level bias analysis with user perception data, this study identifies the empirical foundations necessary for future EDI-AI co-design frameworks, outlining the sociotechnical dimensions that such frameworks must address to be effective.

title: CityRecast: Suppressing Persistent Artifacts in Generative Satellite 3D Reconstruction
authors: Shuo Cui, Yingyan Hou, Wanxuan Lu, Hongfeng Yu, Daobing Zhang, Xian Sun
