abstract: Satellite-based 3D reconstruction is limited by sparse observations and changes across acquisition dates. Existing methods use generative priors to recover missing visual detail, but ghosting, streaking, and blur persist in their Gaussian scenes. These artifacts become particularly apparent in low-elevation renderings. We introduce CityRecast to suppress these artifacts through Gaussian scene repair and supervision calibration. To correct the Gaussian distributions that produce these artifacts, we first use multi-angle warm-up to constrain their spatial extent. This reduces the initial ghosting carried into progressive refinement. Surface-guided replacement then continues to repair the Gaussian distribution while preserving existing appearance. To provide more reliable supervision for this process, observation calibration mitigates interference from multi-temporal observations. Joint refinement further reduces conflicts among generated views. Experiments on DFC2019 and IARPA demonstrate reduced artifacts in low-elevation renderings while maintaining satellite-view fidelity. Compared with Skyfall-GS, CityRecast reduces FID-CLIP by 25.3% on DFC2019 and 51.8% on IARPA. MUSIQ increases by 14.54 and 24.95 points, respectively.

title: Path-probability gradients for optimizing force fields against dynamical observables
authors: Zhongyao Wang, Lun Song, Yakun Zeng, Xingao Gong, Rui Shi, Mao Su
abstract: Machine learning force fields inherit the errors of the electronic-structure methods used to generate their training data, and refining them against experimental measurements provides a direct route beyond this limit. However, such refinement remains difficult for dynamical observables because differentiating chaotic molecular trajectories yields unstable gradients. Here, we introduce PathGrad, which differentiates Langevin path probabilities instead of the trajectories themselves. The resulting gradient estimator is accumulated on the fly from thermal noise and force derivatives, and its variance remains stable as the trajectory length increases. We validated the gradient estimator against finite-difference calculations and used it to fine-tune molten-copper and water potentials against experimental diffusion coefficients together with structural constraints. For water, jointly optimizing diffusion and the oxygen-oxygen radial distribution function also improves the predictions of shear viscosity and rotational relaxation, neither of which is included in the optimization objective. Alignment at a single temperature also improves the apparent activation energies of multiple dynamical observables, bringing their temperature dependences closer to experiments. Moreover, the optimized potential exhibits smaller force errors relative to an independent, higher-level quantum-chemical reference, indicating that alignment with experiments improves the fidelity of the potential energy surface beyond the fitted targets. PathGrad thus establishes a general framework for incorporating experimental observables directly into force field optimizations.

title: QoS-Constrained Sum-Rate Maximization in RIS-Assisted Pinching-Antenna NOMA Systems
authors: Lütfullah Özkan, Saliha Büyükçorak
abstract: This paper investigates a two-user downlink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) system jointly assisted by a single-waveguide pinching-antenna system (PASS) and a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). To maximize the achievable sum rate under quality-of-service (QoS) constraints, the pinching antenna (PA) positions, RIS phase shifts, and power allocation coefficients are jointly optimized. The resulting non-convex optimization problem is addressed using an alternating optimization (AO) framework, where power allocation is obtained in closed form, while RIS phase shifts and PA positions are optimized through majorization-minimization (MM) and sequential quadratic programming (SQP), respectively. Numerical results show that the proposed architecture achieves higher sum rates than conventional-antenna and PASS-only benchmarks. Moreover, the MM- and SQP-based optimization stages achieve performance comparable to semidefinite relaxation (SDR) and grid-based exhaustive search, respectively, while the AO algorithm exhibits rapid convergence.

title: Z boson production in lead-lead collisions: An investigation Utilizing MRW nuclear TMDs
authors: S. Rezaie, R. Kord Valeshabadi, K. Azizi
abstract: We investigate $Z$-boson production in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$ within the $k_t$-factorization framework, using four nuclear transverse-momentum-dependent parton distribution (TMD) prescriptions, namely LO-MRW, VO-MRW, MVO-MRW, and MKMRW. The aim of this study is to examine how different ordering conditions and normalization treatments influence the theoretical description of this process. We calculate the rapidity and transverse-momentum distributions using the parton-level KaTie event generator and compare the predictions with CMS measurements and collinear NLO calculations. This comparison allows us to assess the sensitivity of the predicted distributions to the choice of UPDF prescription.

title: CORALIE Radial Velocity Search for Companions around Evolved Stars (CASCADES) VI. Revised masses and homogeneous estimation of the stellar parameters of 583 red giants
authors: Emile Fontanet, Stéphane Udry, Damien Ségransan, Patrick Eggenberger, Pedro Figueira, João P. Faria
abstract: Giant-star radial-velocity surveys allow us to study how the exoplanet population varies with stellar mass and evolution. However, obtaining accurate estimates of stellar masses for such stars is challenging, as methods like isochrone fitting are prone to large errors due to the degeneracy associated with the closeness of isochrones. We provide a homogeneous re-derivation of the stellar parameters of the CASCADES giant-star survey. This includes parameters obtained from spectral energy distribution fitting, as well as an update of the stellar masses using asteroseismology. We use TESS light curves to measure the frequency of maximum oscillation power, $ν_{\rm max}$, for all the stars when applicable. We re-extract the stellar radii of the survey by fitting broadband photometry with ARIADNE, a spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting package, using priors from spectroscopy for the effective temperature, metallicity and $\log g$. By using scaling relations, we compute revised estimates of the stellar masses of targets with a $ν_{\rm max}$ measurement. We obtain new estimates of mass for 583 out of the 640 stars of the survey. These revised masses are typically 15 to 20% lower (median difference of $-0.35\,M_\odot$) than the ones obtained by isochrone fitting, in particular for low-metallicity stars for which this effect is stronger. These new masses impact the overall mass distribution of the sample, whose median decreases from $2.11\,M_\odot$ to $1.65\,M_\odot$. These revised masses provide the basis for future occurrence-rate analyses aiming to study the link between host-star mass and planet occurrence. They also highlight the uncertainties associated with the determination of masses for evolved stars.

title: DED-Agent: An agentic AI method for autonomous thermal simulation model development and calibration in laser directed energy deposition
authors: Michael Song, Yilong Dai, Lin Cheng
abstract: In metal additive manufacturing (AM), process parameters set the local thermal history, which governs defects, microstructure and properties. Laser power, scan speed, hatch spacing, layer thickness, scan strategy and position combine into a design space of 10^4-10^6 conditions, which is beyond what human experts can map by hand with finite element (FE) thermal models: every model must be set up, meshed, solved and calibrated by an expert, and calibrating unknown heat-source parameters alone can take days to weeks. This paper presents DED-Agent, an agentic artificial intelligence (AI) method for autonomous simulation model development and calibration in laser directed energy deposition (L-DED). A supervisor agent coordinates three specialist agents that share a structured simulation specification and call open-source tools. An intent agent turns a plain-language request into a validated specification, a simulation agent builds, runs and checks an FE thermal model through physics-aware step-by-step reasoning, and a calibration agent identifies key heat-source parameters against experimental data (e.g., thermocouple data) using a high-order proper generalized decomposition (HOPGD) surrogate within a trust-region search. On five benchmark builds, from single-track walls to a multi-track band on a cylindrical tube, the agents built executable thermal models without manual intervention, with 4.1-9.1% error for the simple and medium builds. Within three calibration rounds, the error fell to 0.9-2.5%. The surrogate matched full FE to within 0.08-1.55% and shortened calibration by 5-13 times. Agentic AI can thus autonomously establish reliable, accurate simulation models for AM processes and accelerate the search for process parameters that control microstructure.

title: Exploiting SU(2) Symmetry for Efficient Quantum State Preparation of Matrix Product States
authors: Etienne D'Argenlieu, Alessandro Summer, François Jamet, David P. Tew, Lachlan P. Lindoy
abstract: Quantum computing offers a promising route to simulating strongly correlated systems, particularly for dynamical and spectral quantities whose classical computation can become prohibitively expensive. Fault-tolerant algorithms for these tasks, including real-time dynamics and phase estimation, assume efficient preparation of the initial many-body state, making state preparation an important bottleneck. Matrix product states obtained classically with the density matrix renormalization group can be compiled sequentially into fault-tolerant circuits. We exploit non-Abelian spin SU(2) symmetry in this compilation. By the Wigner-Eckart theorem, only the reduced tensors, which carry the variational information, need generic unitary synthesis. The magnetic structure is restored by Clebsch-Gordan transformations with analytically known angles. We benchmark the method on representative strongly correlated models, including the one-dimensional Hubbard model, quasi-one-dimensional Hubbard geometries, and Anderson impurity models, and perform fault-tolerant resource estimates using the Toffoli count as the primary cost metric. Across the systems considered, exploiting non-Abelian SU(2) symmetry reduces the Toffoli cost roughly threefold relative to U(1)-adapted compilation and by more than an order of magnitude relative to the standard dense compilation method. These results demonstrate how non-Abelian symmetries can substantially reduce the cost of transferring classically tractable many-body ground states to quantum computers, facilitating their use in quantum dynamics and energy estimation.

title: Exact solution of the Bose-Fermi mixture along the unnesting line
authors: Soham Chandak, Aleksandra Petković, Zoran Ristivojevic
abstract: A one-dimensional model of a Bose-Fermi mixture with contact repulsions is exactly solvable via nested Bethe ansatz. That formal solution is here simplified along a special line where the Bethe-ansatz equations can be unnested. The model solution is expressed in terms of the known solutions for the Lieb-Liniger model and the Yang-Gaudin model of attractive spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ fermions in the balanced case. We find explicit analytical results for the ground-state energy, the velocities of excitations, and the Drude weights at weak and strong interactions. At weak interactions, the special line corresponds to the parameter values where the isolated systems of free fermions and weakly interacting bosons have equal velocities.

title: Sample-Efficient In-Context Adaptation via Sleep
authors: Sangyun Lee, Zhang Enyan, Michael Xu, Hao Tang, Zinan Lin, Weijia Xu, Chris Quirk, Jianfeng Gao, Giulia Fanti, Xiaodong Liu
abstract: The ability to learn and generalize from limited experience, or sample efficiency, is a cornerstone of intelligence. How can we build language models that turn a few user interactions, a few snippets of unfamiliar code, or a handful of experimental results provided in context into knowledge that generalizes? Prior work has found that sleep, a process where the model performs $N$ recurrent forward passes to refine its representations of a chunk of context, can improve long-context reasoning (specifically, within SSM-attention hybrid models). We study whether this method also improves in-context adaptation on general, non-synthetic tasks for transformer language models. To this end, we pre-train language models up to 1.2B-parameters on up to 100B tokens with sleep mechanisms. Notably, longer sleep (i.e., using a larger number of recurrent forward passes $N$) enables the model to learn faster in-context on multiple few-shot algorithmic, question-answering tasks, while also achieving lower next-token prediction loss on out-of-distribution evaluations. On held-out code, models with $N=2$ and $N=4$ match the no-sleep baseline's loss using $2.10\times$ and $2.39\times$ fewer tokens in-context, respectively. More broadly, we view our work as a step toward building models that have better tradeoffs between in-context adaptation and decoding latency.

title: Packing the Bragg sphere: complete three-dimensional photonic band gaps at the refractive index of polymers (1.55)
authors: Alexander Itin
abstract: Complete 3D photonic band gaps have so far been found only at refractive-index contrasts of about 1.9 and above, reached by rod-connected diamond lattice structures. Reciprocal-space design of quasiperiodic structures recently achieved considerable emission attenuation at much lower contrasts [L. Maiwald et al., Adv. Optical Mater. 10, 2100785 (2022)]. Here we implement systematic search and reciprocal-space design of periodic 3D structures with complete band gaps, solving a discrete optimization problem on an integer lattice. A gap above a high band needs the strongest Fourier components of the dielectric close to the Bragg sphere of that band. Crystals with large cells, started from Fourier peaks at the vertices of a polyhedron on this sphere and optimized against densely refined band edges, open complete gaps down to an index contrast of 1.55, that of common polymers against air. A rational approximant of an icosidodecahedron gave the most efficient location of the Fourier peaks among the polyhedra tested. Numerical calculations confirm the gaps over a resolution series, with band edges searched over the whole Brillouin zone. The best designs are connected porous networks, suited to a microwave test with printed polymer. A rigorous bound, valid for any structure, does not exclude gaps at lower index, and the next rational approximants of the icosidodecahedron, whose Bragg zones match bands 576 and 2440 almost exactly, point to where gaps at even lower contrast may be sought.

title: Dynamical conditions for tilting Neptune during planetary migration
authors: Andrea Moretti, Giacomo Lari
abstract: Giant planets are expected to form with near-zero obliquities, so that their current tilts must be the result of some post-formation processes. Capture into spin-orbit resonances has been shown to provide a viable mechanism for explaining the current obliquities of Jupiter, Saturn, and Uranus. We aim to determine whether specific configurations of a primordial satellite system of Neptune could have enabled the tilting of its spin axis during planetary migration. We modeled Neptune's secular spin-axis dynamics, including the presence of a primordial satellite system that enhanced the planet's precession constant. We numerically explored the conditions on the primordial satellite system that could trigger a spin-orbit resonance. We identified an open set in the parameter space that led to a successful tilting of Neptune. In particular, the total mass of the primordial system must have been $\geq 4\times 10^{-4}\,M_N$. A representative configuration consists of an inner satellite of mass $5\times 10 ^{-5}\,M_N$ and semi-major axis $35\,R_N$, and an outer satellite of mass $3.5\times 10 ^{-4}\,M_N$ and semi-major axis $100\,R_N$. Such a system could have survived during the unstable phase of the planetary migration if the gravitational encounters between Neptune and Uranus were not too close. The eventual ejection of the outer moon, possibly due to the encounter with a planetesimal, froze Neptune's obliquity to its current value. Neptune's current obliquity can be attained during planetary migration if the planet initially possessed a satellite system with a suitable architecture. The required satellite properties are not far from theoretical predictions and are consistent with recent scenarios proposed for the tilting of Uranus. Once the outer moon was ejected, the system matched a configuration suitable for the following capture of Triton and its fast evolution toward its current orbit.

title: Mixed local and fractional laplacian problems with $(α,β)$-Neumann conditions
authors: Umberto Guarnotta, Salvatore A. Marano, Olimpio H. Miyagaki
abstract: The existence of non-constant solutions to a mixed local-nonlocal elliptic problem with $(α,β)$-Neumann conditions, critical exponent, and parameter $λ>0$ is established for any $λ$ large enough. Proofs exploit both mountain-pass-type arguments and appropriate boundary Sobolev inequalities patterned after those of [19].

title: Beyond Static Semantics: Instance-Adaptive Vision-Language Alignment for Building Damage Assessment
authors: Hang Yin, Jiepan Li, Hongruixuan Chen, Guangyi Yang, Wei He
abstract: Instance-level building damage assessment (IBDA) from bi-temporal remote sensing imagery remains challenging, as the same damage grade may exhibit diverse visual manifestations across individual buildings. Natural language offers explicit descriptions of physical damage, providing complementary semantic cues beyond discrete category labels. However, existing vision--language approaches have not fully addressed how damage semantics should adapt to local bi-temporal evidence and subsequently serve as instance-specific references for severity discrimination. To bridge this gap, we propose LAMIA-IBDA, a unified vision--language framework that progressively grounds shared damage semantics in local observations and individual buildings. Specifically, Adaptive Text-Visual Alignment (ATVA) enables evidence-adaptive semantic interaction by jointly contextualizing multiple damage descriptions and bi-temporal visual features under reliability-aware attention supervision. Dynamic Instance-Prototype Grounding (DIPG) further associates these contextualized semantics with individual building regions to construct instance-adaptive prototypes for fine-grained damage classification. Instance-level description preferences additionally supervise fusion-stage attention, linking semantic adaptation with instance discrimination. Extensive experiments on xBD and BRIGHT demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across optical--optical and optical--SAR settings. The source code is publicly available https://github.com/Cutensil/LAMIA-IBDA.

title: Quadratic Wasserstein transport for elliptical distributions
authors: Jonathan Ansari, Ludger Rüschendorf
abstract: The quadratic Wasserstein distance between Gaussian distributions is given by the classical Bures-Wasserstein formula, which depends only on the means, the covariance matrices $Σ_0$ and $Σ_1$, and their interaction $K=(Σ_0^{1/2}Σ_1Σ_0^{1/2})^{1/2}$. The same formula holds for elliptical distributions with a common radial law. In this paper, we extend this representation to general elliptical distributions by identifying an additional transport cost $Γ$ that depends on the radial laws and the spectrum of $K$. We describe $Γ$ via a weighted quadratic transport problem involving Dirichlet distributions and show that optimal couplings preserve directions within the eigenspaces of $K$. When $K$ has a single eigenvalue, we obtain an explicit cost formula and an optimal Monge map. For general spectra, we derive remarkably tight lower and upper bounds for $Γ$ using nested spectral projections and Knothe-Rosenblatt couplings. The lower bound is based on one-dimensional integrals and can be computed fast. For Gaussian, Student-$t$, uniform ball, and uniform sphere distributions, the upper bound also admits computationally efficient representations via dynamic programming. Numerical experiments demonstrate that we reduce the gap between the previously known bounds by more than 80% in many settings, and by over 99.9% in certain scenarios, even in dimension $10^6$. These improvements are particularly valuable in high-dimensional or heavy-tailed settings, where accurate numerical computation of quadratic Wasserstein distances is challenging.

title: RubikSQL-HB: Agentic Text-to-SQL with Knowledge in the Loop
authors: Haorui Jia, Zihan Qu, Yundi Dong, Ziyang Mei, Chi Zhang, Zezhi Zheng, Dousheng Zhao, Jiahao Zhang, Zui Chen, Han Li
abstract: Database agents need more than schema structure: business meanings, stored values and reference queries supply knowledge that becomes relevant at different points in reasoning. We introduce RubikSQL-HB, which exposes these materials through queryable, database-specific knowledge workspaces built on the HeavenBase platform. Its knowledge interface remains available as an agent constructs and investigates an answer. Candidate agents interleave knowledge access with SQL construction and execution; a downstream Judge can reuse the same interfaces to investigate disagreements. A two-stage example interface separates discovering a reference question from expanding its SQL. On a 500-question BIRD Mini-Dev evaluation, the full pipeline reaches 75.2% execution accuracy, against 71.2% for first-candidate selection and 70.4% for execution-majority voting, with a correct candidate available on 79.0% of questions. The raw-knowledge condition, which also regenerates candidates without the built workspace, is 3.0 points lower, and adjudication with tools and revision accounts for most of the gain over selection baselines. A recorded execution probe shows how continued investigation resolves a candidate disagreement. Separate archived runs show semantic revision recovering answers absent from their original candidate pools. A versioned development study further illustrates how recurring corrections become reusable execution checks. The system and results connect knowledge-interface design to agent decision quality: queryable knowledge supports the construction of useful alternatives, and evidence-aware adjudication connects those alternatives to a final answer. Keeping knowledge in the loop lets agents acquire relevant observations as their reasoning develops.

title: Twisted $L^2$-torsion functions obstruct fibring over the circle
authors: Sam Hughes, Wolfgang Lueck
abstract: The vanishing of the L^2-Betti numbers of the universal covering of a closed manifold is an obstruction to fibring over the circle. When the L^2-Betti numbers vanish we introduce a secondary obstruction based on the asymptotic behaviour of the twisted L^2-torsion function at 0 and infinity. We provide a number of examples showing the invariant is indeed non-trivial.

title: A $2$-adic Kida-type formula for chromatic Selmer groups of elliptic curves and applications to quadratic twists
authors: Taiga Adachi
abstract: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ with good supersingular reduction at $2$. We study the chromatic ($\sharp/\flat$) Selmer groups of $E$ over the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_2$-extension of $\mathbb{Q}$, defined using Sprung's chromatic Coleman maps. We show that at least one of these Selmer groups is $Λ$-cotorsion and, assuming the vanishing of the corresponding $μ$-invariant, establish a $2$-adic Kida-type formula describing the change in the Iwasawa $λ$-invariants under base change from $\mathbb{Q}$ to a real quadratic field $F$ in which $2$ is unramified. When $E$ has square-free conductor, applying this formula to $E$ and its quadratic twist $E^D$ yields an explicit formula describing the variation of the chromatic $λ$-invariants under twists by positive square-free integers $D\equiv1\pmod4$. As an application, under suitable hypotheses on the root number and chromatic Iwasawa invariants of $E$, we construct explicit sets of primes $\ell$ such that the $2^{\infty}$-Selmer group of $E^{\ell}$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ has $\mathbb{Z}_2$-corank one, and determine their positive natural densities.

title: Emerging International Best Practices for AI Model Specs
authors: Edward Kembery, Nathan Lambert, Robert McCarthy, Jinge Wang, Peng Xu, Naying Hu, Clement Neo, Xu Jia, Miro Pluckebaum, Seán Ó hÉigeartaigh, Sören Mindermann, Christoph Winter, Lujain Ibrahim, Yawen Duan, Saad Siddiqui
abstract: Frontier AI developers from around the world have begun to publish documents that describe how their AI models are intended to behave. Although these 'model specifications'-or 'model specs', for short-are increasingly important in AI development and governance, little independent guidance exists for writing them. This paper addresses this gap in five main sections. First, we outline the advantages of writing a model spec for AI developers and society at large. Second, we introduce a taxonomy for model specs that developers can take inspiration from. Third, we propose guidance for writing and implementing a spec in practice. Fourth, we note eight open problems related to writing model specs for safe and desirable behaviour. We conclude with recommendations for frontier AI companies, governments, and research and civil society organisations.

title: A Barsotti-Weil isomorphism for Taelman units
authors: Quentin Gazda
abstract: The positive-characteristic analogue of motivic cohomology with coefficients in an Anderson A-motive M over a function field of transcendence degree one was introduced in an earlier work of the author. In this paper, we prove that, when M arises as the dual of the A-motive of an Anderson module E that is abelian, uniformizable, and has everywhere good reduction, the corresponding A-motivic cohomology coincides with the module of Taelman units of E, up to a twist by the module of Kähler differentials of A. To this end, we recast the theory of Anderson generating functions in the spirit of earlier work of Maurischat and the author on special functions.

title: Programmable multipartite entanglement analogues
authors: Long Chen, Qing Chun Yin, Zi Xuan Cai, Zhou He, Zhi Cai Yu, Zhihao Lan, Xiaohan Cui, Jian Wei You, Tie Jun Cui
abstract: Quantum entanglement underpins the quantum information science. Its multipartite forms distribute coherence across several subsystems, but controlling their composition and order is increasingly difficult as more subsystems participate. Classical nonseparable waves provide accessible analogues of these structures, although existing implementations largely fix the participating degrees of freedom through their generating architectures. Here we overcome this constraint by making multipartiteness itself programmable in electromagnetic fields. A spatiotemporal metasurface reconfigures the identity and number of coherently linked state spaces independently across polarization, frequency, orbital angular momentum, wavevector direction, and orthogonal envelope modes. We realize complete Bell-like and Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-like families from bipartite to five-partite order and exchange constituents at fixed order. To our knowledge, the five-partite state has the highest multipartite order experimentally realized in classical electromagnetic fields. These results establish the distribution of coherence across physical state spaces as a programmable property of classical waves and provide a platform for studying selected structures of multipartite quantum states without invoking quantum entanglement or nonlocality.

title: Low-Power Spiking Neural Network Acceleration with Differential Time Representation: A Modular Hardware Framework
authors: Daniel Windhager, Lothar Ratschbacher, Bernhard A. Moser, Michael Lunglmayr
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer promising energy efficiency, making them well suited for energy-constrained applications. Much of their energy savings stems from the sparse encoding of spike trains. We show that spike trains can be represented more efficiently using Differential Time Representation (DTR), which requires fewer bits than Address-Event Representation (AER) or equidistantly sampled 1-bit spike trains. To support multiple input spike trains, we provide a rigorous proof that DTR sequences can be merged with low complexity. We also provide a set of modular hardware streaming components using this representation that can be flexibly connected to construct custom accelerator architectures for specific SNNs. Tailoring the hardware architecture to the selected SNN is streamlined by a Python framework combining the modular hardware components into a full SNN implementation. We use the framework to generate three accelerators for the Spiking Heidelberg Digits (SHD), Spiking Speech Commands (SSC), and PSMNIST benchmarks, each in a throughput-optimized parallel variant and a resource-reduced time-multiplexed variant. We report results for FPGA and ASIC implementations, the latter synthesized with a fully open-source flow targeting the predictive ASAP7 PDK. On the SHD dataset, the ASIC implementation reaches 92.46% classification accuracy, while sustaining $\approx{}$12,027 inferences per second at 20.37$μ$J per inference, exceeding the neuromorphic Loihi processor by 109$\times$ in throughput and 1.8$\times$ in energy efficiency. The corresponding FPGA implementation achieves $\approx{}$6,023 inferences per second without using DSP blocks. Across all three datasets, the synthesized ASICs reduce energy per inference by 27-37$\times$ relative to their FPGA counterparts, demonstrating that competitive SNN accelerators can be realized entirely within an open-source design flow.

title: Variance Reduction Note 5: The Convergence of Loopless SVRG
authors: Kamran Fareed, Alina Lodhi
abstract: A snapshot in loopless SVRG has no prescribed lifetime. At each step the algorithm may keep using an old full gradient or compute a new one. How does this choice enter the convergence proof, and how often is a new full gradient worth its cost? For a strongly convex finite sum we follow the age and objective gap of the snapshot. Its expected gap is a geometrically weighted average of earlier iterate gaps. This identity determines a weight for the snapshot in a one-step contraction argument and gives an objective bound for the last iterate. A two-component quadratic makes the estimator variance explicit, including on the step immediately after a refresh. We also evaluate the work bound as a function of the refresh probability and compare its minimizer with the condition-number-independent choice $p=1/n$.

title: Baker-Akhiezer functions for Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system
authors: Liudmila Bishler
abstract: The Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system is a counterpart of the trigonometric Ruijsenaars integrable system (associated with the root system $A_n$) for the root system $(C_n^\vee, C_n)$. It depends on the standard Macdonald parameters $q$ and $t$ as well as the Koornwinder (Askey-Wilson) parameters $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$. Different specializations of the parameters connect it to the other classical root systems from the $(C_n^\vee, C_n)$ family. The eigenfunctions of the Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system are the symmetric Koornwinder polynomials; for certain values of the parameters $t$, $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ they coincide with the sum over the Weyl group of the Baker-Akhiezer functions introduced by O.A.\,Chalykh for the classical root system $BC_n$. The main idea behind this paper is to elucidate Chalykh's formalism and apply it to other affine root systems. We define Baker-Akhiezer functions for all root systems in the $(C_n^\vee, C_n)$ family. We also present some explicit expressions for Baker-Akhiezer functions.

title: Fluctuations in the k-cut numbers of random recursive trees
authors: Laura Eslava, Marco L. Ortiz, Minmin Wang
abstract: We consider the k-cut procedure introduced by Cai et al. [EJP, 2018] on random recursive trees. Our main result identifies the fluctuations in the number of cuts required to isolate the root as the tree size tends to infinity. This extends the results by Drmota et al. [RSA, 2009] and Iksanov et al. [ECP, 2007] for the classical cutting procedure.

title: A Gauge Pathway to an Ultralight Axion through a Hidden Portal
authors: Claudio Corianø`
abstract: We study a gauge realization of an ultralight axion with a hidden $SU(2)$ interaction, an Abelian vector portal, a charged Higgs and a Stückelberg field. The vector absorbs one scalar combination and leaves a physical phase. Its normalization is fixed by the Higgs and Stückelberg scales, while hidden confinement generates its mass. Keeping this phase ultralight requires an additional symmetry: the displayed gauge charges alone allow large phase-dependent scalar interactions. We quantify the suppression required of these interactions. Pure-$SU(2)$ lattice results relate the susceptibility to physical confinement scales; one- and two-loop running illustrate the dependence on the chosen high-energy coupling. We derive the coherent radiation-era density and exhibit an initial angle giving the reference dark-matter abundance for $F_χ\simeq10^{17}\,\GeV$ and zero-temperature mass $m_{χ,0}=3\times10^{-20}\,\eV$. We follow the confined population through number-changing and number-conserving limits and bound its energy contribution. An illustrative inflaton background satisfies the stated vacuum and isocurvature tests, conditional on control of a large portal correction to its potential. Its cold hidden history requires a hidden-to-visible reheating fraction near $5\times10^{-12}$, whose microscopic origin remains an input. A second, gauge-anomaly-free model gives the same physical phase scale using two charged Higgs singlets. These constructions specify conditional cosmological examples and the additional protection and reheating mechanisms needed to complete them.

title: Conformality lost in Anderson localization in infinite dimensions, and regained in finite dimensions: a phenomenological theory of the Anderson transition in high dimensions
authors: Antonello Scardicchio, Carlo Vanoni
abstract: We show that the recent works on Anderson localization when the number of spatial dimensions $d\to\infty$ can be framed into the scenario dubbed it conformality lost [Kaplan et al., Phys. Rev. D 80, 125005 (2009)], which occurs when two fixed points of the RG collide and become complex. This framing makes it natural for a two-parameter scaling flow à la Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless (BKT) to control all the observables of the theory as conjectured in [Vanoni et al., PNAS 121, e2401955121 (2024)]. We also use this as a starting point for an $ε$ expansion of the RG equations in $ε=1/d\ll 1$, and find phenomenological RG equations which fit the numerical results in dimensions $d\gtrsim 4$.

title: Mixing and Preserving Properties of Non-van der Waals 2D Materials in Sandwich-like Heterostructures
authors: Anastasiia Nihei, Rico Friedrich
abstract: Heterostructure interfaces created by stacking two-dimensional (2D) materials outline an appealing route towards achieving advanced electronic and magnetic functionalities at the nanoscale. Non-van der Waals (non-vdW) sandwich-like heterostructures (HSs) are build out of non-vdW 2D materials derived from non-layered crystals and establish a new frontier enabling strong interfacial coupling. Employing ab initio density functional theory (DFT), we investigate two classes of such trilayer HSs: purely non-vdW assemblies and hybrid vdW/non-vdW/vdW stacks. We show that non-vdW sandwiches undergo pronounced geometric reconstruction forming chemically bonded interfaces with large absolute binding energies up to an order of magnitude larger than those of conventional vdW HSs. These strong interactions drive extensive electronic hybridization, band gap renormalization, and tunable interlayer magnetic coupling. In contrast, vdW encapsulation largely protects the intrinsic atomic and electronic structure of the non-vdW sheet from the environment , while enabling charge transfer doping of the vdW layers. Our results thus establish sandwich HSs a versatile interface design platform, spanning interaction regimes from weakly perturbed encapsulation to strongly interacting chemically bonded systems with emergent electronic and magnetic behavior.

title: ViDM: Efficient and Order-Robust Parallel Visual Decision Making
authors: Xudong Tan, Peng Ye, Chenyu Huang, Yaoxin Yang, Huafeng Qin, Tao Chen
abstract: Visual decision-making demands accurate judgments and timely responses. Yet for multiple questions sharing the same visual input, autoregressive multimodal large language models generate answers token by token, accumulating sequential decoding costs as question count grows and delaying completion of the decision set. Their predictions can also vary with question order. We introduce ViDM, which transforms multi-question visual inference into parallel decisions in a single forward pass, improving both accuracy and inference efficiency. ViDM organizes shared visual context, multiple questions, and question-specific decision slots into one sequence, reusing the native language-model head to produce all answer distributions simultaneously. A Decision-Query Mask aligns each decision query's direct attention with shared context and its corresponding question, while case-balanced multi-order training strengthens robustness to question reordering. Across nine benchmarks spanning image, multi-image, and video tasks, ViDM improves Qwen3.5-4B's average accuracy from 73.49% to 77.55% while achieving 8.4x the baseline's average end-to-end throughput. On GQA, where each evaluated image has 11.4 questions on average, the end-to-end speedup reaches 20.3x. ViDM also improves mean and worst-order accuracy while reducing order-induced variation across multiple benchmarks, with further validation on LLaVA-OneVision-7B and InternVL3.5-4B.

title: Do Layer Rankings Survive Silence Trimming? The Silence Shortcut in Frozen WavLM Representations for Audio Deepfake Detection
authors: Nur Elabid, Mahmud Esad Arar
abstract: Layer-wise analyses of frozen self-supervised encoders are used to locate spoofing information in audio deepfake detection. On the ASVspoof 2019 logical access (LA) benchmark, bonafide recordings carry longer leading and trailing silence than spoofed ones, and detectors exploit this cue, the silence shortcut. This paper examines whether layer rankings for a frozen WavLM Base encoder survive the trimming of this silence. A small classifier is trained on each of the 12 layers with and without trimming and evaluated on ASVspoof 2019 LA and, zero-shot, on In-the-Wild, in all four train/test combinations, with speaker-level bootstrap intervals. Trimming at 40 dB raises the in-domain error at every layer and preserves the layer ranking only partly (Kendall's tau of 0.58 in domain, 0.73-0.76 on In-the-Wild). The best layer is unchanged at 40 dB, but on the evaluation set it moves from layer 5 to layer 6 at 15 dB and, with mean pooling, at 20 dB, thresholds at which trimming may also remove low-energy speech. At 40 dB, the equal error rate of a model trained with silence rises by 6.3-19.9 percentage points at every layer when only its test audio is trimmed. On In-the-Wild, the effect depends on the layer: at layers 3-5, trimming the test audio lowers the error only for models trained on trimmed audio, whereas at layers 6, 8, and 9 training on trimmed audio lowers it also on clean test audio. We quantify how zero padding alters WavLM features through group normalization, an effect that an attention mask does not fully undo.

title: A Mesh to Remember: Persistent Appearance for Interactive Video Worlds
authors: Joonghyuk Shin, Alex Trevithick, Katarína Tóthová, Liyuan Zhu, Shengyu Huang, Jaesik Park, Shalini De Mello, Laura Leal-Taixé, Riccardo de Lutio, Haithem Turki
abstract: Video world models synthesize photorealistic observations in response to user actions but struggle to remain consistent over long interactions. Coding agents and text-to-3D models instead generate explicit 3D worlds whose geometry and state persist by construction, but whose appearance falls far short of photorealism. Recent methods combine the strengths of both by rendering such worlds into coarse proxies that guide a video model. However, since these proxies only specify where things are, the renderer must invent what they look like as the world is explored, and anything it forgets is reinvented when a surface reappears. Our key insight is that a mesh identifies which surface each pixel shows, across frames and views, even as objects move, allowing it to serve as an address for what the renderer generates. We propose M2R (Mesh to Remember), a few-step causal video renderer that stores its own features on the surfaces they depict, in each object's frame, and retrieves them by rasterizing the mesh whenever those surfaces come back into view. Appearance thus travels with objects wherever they move, persists across revisits, and is shared by every agent that observes it, while memory grows with the surfaces seen instead of the number of frames. Trained only on synthetic data, M2R transfers zero-shot to real indoor scans and to worlds authored by coding agents. It outperforms state-of-the-art methods in consistency across static, dynamic, and multi-agent benchmarks, more than doubling object permanence and nearly doubling cross-agent consistency, while rendering 720p video in real time (40 FPS).

title: Entanglement island and Page curve for one-sided rotating Kerr black holes
authors: Soumen Pari
abstract: We investigate the information paradox for one-sided asymptotically flat rotating Kerr black holes formed through gravitational collapse using the island prescription. Near the horizon, the dynamics of a scalar field can be described by an effective two-dimensional theory, which provides the framework for our analysis. We study how rotation affects the location of the island boundary $\partial I$, the Page time, and the scrambling time, treating non-extremal and extremal Kerr black holes separately. For non-extremal black holes, the emergence of an island prevents the unbounded growth of Hawking radiation entropy at late times and restores the unitary Page curve. We further find that the island boundary depends on the location of the cutoff surface, in contrast to the behaviour found for eternal Kerr black holes. In the extremal case, the late-time entanglement entropy of Hawking radiation approaches the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of the extremal black hole. Our results demonstrate the important role of black hole geometry in determining the behaviour of entanglement entropy and suggest that the island prescription provides a semiclassical resolution of the information paradox for one-sided rotating Kerr black holes.

title: Romans Mass from a $\mathrm{GL}(1,\mathbb{R})$ Topological Field Theory with Boundary
authors: Euihun Joung, J. A. Rosabal
abstract: We construct an eleven-dimensional topological field theory with boundary whose edge modes are the dilaton and form fields of type IIA supergravity, including the Romans mass. The bulk action is the Chern--Simons functional of the superalgebra of the doubled formalism, completed by two brackets that are invisible in ten dimensions; it is unique up to normalization, contains no potentials, and the metric enters only through a boundary term. The Romans mass is the boundary value of a zero-form, like the other field strengths: it is varied, and its equation of motion is an eleven-form Gauss law with no ten-dimensional counterpart. The boundary term breaks the $GL(1,\mathbb{R})$ gauge symmetry to $O(1)$: the dilaton is the edge mode on $GL(1,\mathbb{R})/O(1)$, and $(-1)^{F_L}$, which reverses the Romans mass, becomes a gauge symmetry. The holonomies of the flat connection are monodromies of the dilaton and of $(-1)^{F_L}$, fixed classically by the D8-brane charges when the mass is nonzero, and the hypersurface dual to the $O(1)$ holonomy can end on reflection seven-branes. Since no field is self-dual, the reduction gives Romans' action off shell, while other boundary conditions of the same bulk give massless type IIA and dual formulations.

title: Trace-defined double covers of the $S_3$-involution graph of $PSL_2(2^n)$
authors: G. A. Glinskikh, L. Yu. Tsiovkina
abstract: For $q=2^n\ge 4$, we construct a family of Deza double covers $Γ(q,ξ)$ of the $S_3$-involution graph of $PSL_2(q)$, parametrized by $ξ\in\mathbb F_q^*$. We show that each resulting cover is connected, arc-transitive and amply regular with parameters $(2(q^2-1),q,Tr(ξ),1)$, where $Tr$ denotes the absolute trace. We also show that the trace-one covers are antipodal of diameter $5$ and girth $3$, whereas the trace-zero covers are non-antipodal of diameter $3$ and girth $5$. For $q=4$, these cases yield the well-known icosidodecahedral and dodecadodecahedral graphs, respectively. Then we determine the distance distributions and full automorphism groups of the covers and prove that, for fixed $q$, two covers are isomorphic if and only if their defining parameters lie in the same Frobenius orbit. We also express the Ramanujan property of a cover in terms of the spectral norm of a signed adjacency matrix of the base graph.

title: Factorized Context Attention: From Emulated to Native Grid Probing
authors: Mohamed Eltahir, Manar Eyad, Yara Alzahrani, Fatimah Albesher, Duaa M. Tahir, Tanveer Hussain, Naeemullah Khan
abstract: Models read a book, an hour of video, or an image in one forward pass. As the context grows, this pass slows down, loses accuracy, and stops at the context window. Sparse attention is efficient, but keeps the other two limitations. Grid probing, a recent training-free method, recovers the accuracy and extends the reach by asking a frozen model the same question about short local and strided spans of the input, but every question repeats the whole computation, since each span is encoded again. Our insight is that grid probing is emulated attention, an attention pattern reproduced from outside the model through prompts, since each probe only restricts which part of the input the question can see. We introduce Factorized Context Attention (FCA), a training-free block-sparse attention that runs the same pattern natively, as the attention of the model itself. FCA encodes the input once into a KV cache, reads all spans as masked sequences in one batched forward, and uses a stair position schedule to keep every span inside the trained position range. Across long video understanding, long-context text inference and image grounding, FCA matches the accuracy and the reach of grid probing at a fraction of its cost. It gains about 10 points over the single pass on long video and 9 to 14 points on long novels, finds needles in videos of over a thousand frames and in texts four times the length of the window, and answers a later question about the same input in as little as a tenth of the time of grid probing. Native attention thus keeps what emulated attention gains without its cost, all with existing frozen language and vision-language models.

title: Gradient Descent Achieves $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-7/4})$ Convergence
authors: Chang He, Xiaotian Jiang
abstract: We propose a deterministic stepsize rule for gradient descent on a lower-bounded nonconvex function with Lipschitz-continuous gradient and Hessian. Classical analysis shows that a fixed stepsize guarantees a decrease of order $\varepsilon^2/L$ per update. In contrast, our rule uses a sequence of $\mathcal{O}(m)$ updates with a total stepsize of order $m^2/L$. We establish a weighted descent inequality for every prefix of the update sequence on a quadratic objective and control the error caused by Hessian variation on a general objective. This error determines the choice $m\asymp(L^2/(ρ\varepsilon))^{1/4}$ for small $\varepsilon$. We show that gradient descent with our stepsize rule finds an $\varepsilon$-stationary point within $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-7/4})$ gradient evaluations, matching the optimal gradient-complexity guarantee.

title: A General Framework for Identifying the Joint Potential Outcome Distribution through Support Restrictions
authors: Benedikt Koch, Kosuke Imai
abstract: Many causal estimands depend on the joint distribution of potential outcomes, which is generally not identifiable because only one potential outcome can be observed for each unit. To obtain identification, researchers often impose assumptions such as monotonicity and exclusion restriction that constrain the support of this joint distribution. For treatments and outcomes that each take finitely many values, we define a similarity matrix whose entries count, for each pair of potential outcome strata, the number of treatments yielding the same outcome. We then prove that, under unconfoundedness, identification holds if and only if this matrix is invertible, yielding a criterion directly verifiable from the support. In addition, we derive an identification formula for the joint distribution under these support restrictions and show that an average causal estimand is identifiable if and only if its integrand admits an additive representation on the restricted support. Finally, we derive sharp testable implications of the support restriction. Our results unify and generalize a broad range of identification results in the literature.

title: Beyond Average Gains: Probing the Equity--Vulnerability Tension in Structured Visual AI for Learning
authors: Mingyuan Li, Duan Wang, Erick Purwanto, Yihong Wang
abstract: Open-ended conversational AI requires learners to formulate questions, organize learning paths, and track changing problem states. Structured visual interfaces may ease these demands, but higher average ratings do not establish that support is experienced consistently across learner backgrounds and devices. We conducted a randomized study of graph-algorithm learning, comparing VisualCodeChat (VCC), which combines predefined learning stages, conversational explanations, and dynamic algorithm visualizations, with a standard text-based chatbot. We analyzed 282 post-task questionnaires from university students. In unadjusted comparisons, VCC received significantly higher usability and perceived effectiveness ratings. We detected no significant between-condition differences in efficiency, satisfaction, or post-use emotion. Exploratory within-condition analyses identified differences associated with prior chatbot experience: infrequent users reported lower adoption and learning-management ratings in the standard AI condition, while uncomfortable prior chatbot experiences were associated with lower interaction and layout ratings in the VCC condition. These findings suggest that improving the average interaction experience is only part of making AI-supported learning inclusive. Future evaluations should examine whether learners with different prior experiences can obtain guidance, recover from difficulties, and demonstrate understanding independently across devices.

title: Open-OmniCoach: Evidence-Enhanced Trajectory Learning for Omni Video Agents
authors: Weisong Liu, Xiangtai Li, Haochen Wang, Haiquan Wen, Zhaoxiang Zhang
abstract: Training capable omni video agents requires more than diverse question-answer pairs: agents must learn to reliably find, connect, and correct task-relevant evidence in omni-setting. However, we argue that existing data pipelines provide limited control over task-relevant evidence and weak supervision for these capabilities. In this work, we present Open OmniCoach, a new framework for evidence-seeking omni video agents. It contains a high-quality dataset, OmniCoach-240K, and a new agentic reinforcement learning (RL) method, Step-Level Evidence-Guided Policy Optimization (SEPO). For the former, OmniCoach-240K comprises 248.2K interaction trajectories, including 230.7K multi-span trajectories and 17.4K reflection trajectories. We design a three-stage data pipeline by leveraging both fine-grained omni-evidence and the agent's own errors. Meanwhile, compared with other RL baselines, SEPO provides turn-level credit based on improvements in evidence coverage and temporal localization. Applying both trajectory data and the SEPO method, we obtain Open OmniAgent models. The resulting models outperform the baselines across multiple video and audio-visual understanding tasks by significant margins, demonstrating the effectiveness of the Open OmniCoach framework. In particular, Open OmniAgent-30B improves average accuracy over Qwen3-Omni by 6.3 percentage points across nine benchmarks, with gains of 12.2 and 13.3 points on LVOmniBench and LVBench, respectively.

title: Mixed moment of twisted modular $L$-functions and Dirichlet $L$-functions
authors: Zhaoyan Chen
abstract: Let $f$ be a Hecke holomorphic cusp form for $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$. Let $q=p^γ$ be a prime power, where $p$ is an arbitrary prime and $γ\geq 2$. We establish an asymptotic formula for the mixed moment of $L(s,f\otimesχ)$ and $L(s,χ)$ on the central point. We also establish an upper bound for the smoothed sum of Hecke eigenvalues twisted by hyper-Kloosterman sums modulo powers of $2$.

title: Weighted pointwise estimates for the damped wave equation and global solutions to Nakao's problem in three dimensions
authors: Vladimir Georgiev, Kosuke Kita
abstract: In this paper, we establish weighted pointwise estimates for the Duhamel term of the three-dimensional damped wave equation. The estimates combine the parabolic weight $\langle t+|x|^2\rangle$ with the wave-cone weight $\langle t-|x|\rangle$, and thereby account for both the diffusive part of the damped wave flow and source terms with wave-like decay. As an application, we study Nakao's problem, a weakly coupled system consisting of one semilinear damped wave equation and one semilinear wave equation. Under explicit conditions on the exponents of nonlinear terms, we prove small-data global existence and uniqueness of mild solutions in weighted $L^\infty$ spaces. The result covers both the full parabolic decay and slower pointwise decay for the damped-wave component, and allows either the standard wave decay or slower pointwise decay for the wave component. The proof combines the new Duhamel estimate with weighted estimates for the free wave equation and a contraction argument.

title: Accelerating Equivariant Interatomic Potentials for Molecular Dynamics through Radial tabulation and Kernel Fusion
authors: Jaekyun Yoo, Suyeon Ju
abstract: Equivariant machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) achieve near-quantum-chemical accuracy, but their computational cost and GPU memory footprint restrict molecular dynamics (MD) at extended length and time scales. Even when the tensor product (TP) is accelerated, both bottlenecks remain governed by evaluating and storing per-edge radial weights in the NequIP convolution. We introduce JET-MLIPs (Joint-Kernel Equivariant Convolution with Tabulated Radial Weights for MLIP simulation), a GPU backend applicable to pretrained NequIP-family potentials without retraining. JET-MLIPs replaces the radial multilayer perceptron (MLP) with a piecewise cubic Hermite table and fuses table lookup, spherical harmonics, TP and neighbor aggregation into a single kernel, eliminating per-edge radial-weight and MLP-intermediate storage during force evaluation. Across 15 released potentials from SevenNet, MACE, NequIP-OAM, Nequix and EquFlash on a 5632-atom liquid electrolyte, LAMMPS MD attains 1.5-5.9$\times$ step-time speed-ups and 2.4-24$\times$ peak memory reductions relative to each family's existing TP-accelerated backend on a single H200 GPU while preserving single-precision (fp32) accuracy and dynamical stability. These reductions enable multi-nanosecond transport-property simulations of roughly $10^4$-atom systems on a single GPU and broaden access to large-scale equivariant MLIP MD on widely available GPUs.

title: Sequences for Flat-Top Beams
authors: Cheng Du
abstract: Flat-top beams have numerous applications in radar and communication systems. Sequences with diverging merit factors can approach the ideal omnidirectional beams but do not directly apply to flat-top beams, which require simultaneous control of passband ripple and stopband leakage. To bridge this gap, we study the asymptotic behavior of both quantities of flat-top beams by using tools of Fourier analysis. We establish contrasting results for sequences with finite or infinite alphabets. For sequences with finite alphabet, including binary and quaternary ones, their passband ripple and stopband leakage cannot simultaneously vanish as the sequence length grows to infinity. For sequences with infinite alphabet, however, both requirements are satisfied simultaneously by the generalized step-chirp (GSC) sequences if and only if the length-bandwidth product $Nγ$ goes to infinity and the distance of the step size $a$ from $\{0,1,\tfrac12,\tfrac13,\ldots\}$ goes to zero. Besides, both quantities vanish at rate $O((Nγ)^{-1/2})$ if $a\in \{1,\tfrac12,\tfrac13,\ldots\}$.These results broaden the scope of classical sequence design beyond full-band spectral flatness and provide a theoretical foundation for flat-top beam synthesis.

title: Within-task hazards of AI agents: unidentified by time-horizon curves, identified by repeated runs
authors: Ruiqi Zhao
abstract: The time horizon of an AI agent is read off a curve: the probability that the agent completes a task, plotted against the time a human needs for it. Several recent analyses fit survival models to this curve and conclude that agents' hazard of failure declines as a task goes on. The curve cannot support that conclusion. Every log-logistic horizon curve with slope $β\le1$ is a mixture of constant-hazard curves, and in a proportional-hazards frailty model the same curve is produced by every within-task Weibull shape $k\geβ$. If runs of a task are conditionally independent, repeated runs restore identification within this model: the probability that two runs both succeed is the single-run curve shifted by $1/k$ on the $\log_2$ time axis. Without the Weibull form, the horizontal distance between these two curves still bears on the direction of the hazard: if the average within-task hazard is non-increasing, the distance is at least one, and so is the population limit of a two-step estimator when the cross-section is log-logistic. We decompose the bias of that estimator into a violation of the shift and a first-step misspecification term, and examine five mechanisms that can break the shift. On METR's public run-level data, under stated assumptions that the data cannot verify, no model's 95% interval for $1/k$ lies entirely above one, and for the five frontier models in the TH1.0 release every interval from runs in different batches lies below one. Under the same assumptions, taken interval by interval and given a log-logistic cross-section, these intervals reject a non-increasing average hazard for the five models, whereas in TH1.1 the result depends on how human times were obtained. Whether $k>1$ reflects a hazard that rises within a task or tasks whose difficulty human time measures only loosely needs experiments that observe the same task at several lengths.

title: Continuum model for disconnection structures of hetero-interfaces
authors: Luchan Zhang, Xiaoxue Qin, Dongsong Tao, Jian Han, David J. Srolovitz, Yang Xiang
abstract: Hetero-interfaces, as planar defects between dissimilar materials, accommodate the lattice misfit through networks of line defects of disconnections (a combination of structural ledges/step and dislocation characters). We develop a continuum model that predicts the hetero-interface structures, including disconnection networks, the interface inclination and misorientation angles. The model is based on the interfacial energy minimization with respect to all possible disconnection modes, subject to the interface structure constraint of the generalized Frank-Bilby equation that describes the lattice correspondence across the interface including both dislocation and step characters of disconnections and the inclination and misorientation angles. Numerical simulations are performed to determine the equilibrium configurations of three different types of hetero-interfaces: the $α$/$β$ (orthorhombic/monoclinic) interface in ZrO$_2$, $α$/$β$ hetero-interfaces in Ti and Au/Pd (001) twist-misfit interfaces. Comparisons with experiments, atomistic simulations and theoretical predictions show that our continuum model provides excellent predictions of the hetero-interface structures including disconnection networks and inclination, misorientation angles. Furthermore, systematic analysis reveals the functional dependence of hetero-interface structural properties on inclination and misorientation angles.

title: Every Edit Its Own Budget: Per-Instruction Token Freezing for Training-Free Acceleration of Multi-Edit Image Editing
authors: Jyotirmoy Nath, Neeraj Kumar, Brejesh Lall
abstract: Accelerating instruction-based image editing when one instruction requests several edits is challenging. Many training-free accelerators for flow-matching image editors skip tokens whose prediction has stopped changing, but decide this with a single threshold for the whole image. With several edits, such a threshold, tuned for speed, freezes small and slowly settling edits first, and requested edits disappear. We propose TIDE (Training-free Instruction-aware Drift-based Editing), which gives every instruction part its own compute budget. First, TIDE finds the region of each part in the editor's own attention by unbalanced optimal transport, without masks or external models. Second, it freezes a token once its drift is small relative to its own part and moves it along the straight path to its endpoint estimate. Third, a sparse engine computes only the remaining tokens. We prove that part-agnostic rules cannot guarantee per-part error budgets, characterize the optimal per-part threshold policy up to one tie class per part, and derive when our rule attains it. On FLUX.2 Klein, one global threshold breaks at least one edit's budget in 89% of MICE-Bench images, and TIDE drops up to 77% fewer edits at matched or higher speed (48% on MICE-Bench), a gap human raters confirm. On the many-step Klein Base, TIDE is the fastest compared method on six benchmarks (4.81-4.89x) and needs 5.3x fewer TFLOPs than vanilla, the largest saving we measure. With the same settings, it is also the fastest compared method on Qwen-Image-Edit-2511, a second model family (3.46-3.52x), and drops the fewest edits on all six benchmarks. Code will be made publicly available.

title: Optimal Transport Meets t-SNE: Integrated Visualization without Batch Effects in OT-tSNE
authors: Azhar Akhmetova, Edward Eichhorn, Boris Landa, Dmitry Kobak, Sebastian Damrich
abstract: Visual exploration is an integral step in understanding the structure of datasets. However, systematic variation between datasets collected under different conditions, known as batch effects, can obscure shared structure and complicate their joint visualization. Existing methods often rely on cross-batch nearest-neighbor relations to integrate the batches. Yet, these local correspondences can be unreliable for challenging cross-batch geometries. We propose optimal-transport t-SNE (OT-tSNE), which replaces nearest-neighbor-based matching with globally coupled affinities derived from entropic optimal transport. Controlled synthetic experiments demonstrated that nearest-neighbor-based methods can deteriorate, while optimal-transport affinities and OT-tSNE embeddings remain robust. Across seven real single-cell datasets, we benchmarked OT-tSNE against a broad range of integration and visualization methods and found that it achieves a Pareto-efficient trade-off between batch mixing and biological conservation, and integrates batches particularly well.

title: Not All Pairs Align: Caption-Guided Audio-Visual Contrastive Learning
authors: Omar Emara, Nan Lu, Dima Damen, Hazel Doughty
abstract: We address the problem of learning audio-visual representations from co-occurring modalities. Multimodal contrastive learning typically assumes that paired observations provide shared views of the same underlying information. While this may be true for datasets collected in constrained environments, it does not always hold. For instance, co-occurring audio and visual signals can differ substantially in their content due to off-screen sounds. Nevertheless, standard contrastive objectives treat all paired samples as equally aligned. In this work, we propose Caption Guided Alignment Aware Loss (CGAAL), a model-agnostic objective that leverages modality-specific captions to estimate semantic agreement between audio and video. CGAAL uses these agreement scores to weight the contribution of each positive pair. A warm-up period and gradual thresholding strategy progressively introduce this alignment-aware training signal. We demonstrate the generality of CGAAL by applying it to three contrastive baselines, consistently improving their performance on audio-visual retrieval.

title: PRC4D: Physical Relation-Constrained Persistent 4D Reconstruction
authors: Junho Kim, Hyunyoung Choi, Jiseok Kim, Seongwon Lee
abstract: A faithful 4D reconstruction should capture both the shape and motion of objects, even when they disappear from view. Existing methods preserve previously observed geometry and extend motion through occlusion using local spatial and motion associations. However, treating short-term contact or shared motion as sufficient evidence of persistent rigidity can introduce incorrect motion constraints and distort overall reconstruction. To address this limitation, we present PRC4D, a physical relation-constrained framework that identifies reliable rigid relations and uses them to maintain spatial consistency through occlusion. PRC4D combines 3D contact and relative motion consistency with sequence-level verification to distinguish persistent couplings from transient interactions. The resulting graph guides observed-pose refinement and motion propagation from visible to occluded components without altering reconstructed geometry. Experiments on diverse real-world multi-object sequences and controlled occlusion simulations demonstrate improved reconstruction accuracy, reduced relative pose errors, and more consistent object configurations under changing visibility.

title: Explicit KL Exponents for PLQ Functions on the Sphere
authors: Chen Yanping, Pan Shaohua, Qi Anna
abstract: Let $φ$ be a proper piecewise linear-quadratic (PLQ) function whose domain meets the unit sphere $\mathcal{S}$. We prove that $f:=φ+δ_{\mathcal{S}}$, where $δ_{\mathcal{S}}$ is the indicator function of $\mathcal{S}$, satisfies the Kurdyka--Łojasiewicz (KL) property with exponent $3/4$ throughout its domain. This exponent is sharp even for the convex PLQ class. We characterize the smallest KL exponents of quadratics restricted to affine sections of $\mathcal{S}$, obtaining the values $0$, $1/2$, $2/3$, and $3/4$. A tangential projection identity shows that, at each point of ${\rm dom}\,f$, the maximum of the exponents from the relevant affine sections is admissible for $f$. When $φ$ is piecewise affine (PA), each of these smallest exponents is $0$ or $1/2$. Thus $f$ satisfies the KL property with exponent $1/2$ throughout ${\rm dom}\,f$, and this exponent is sharp over the class of sphere-constrained PA functions. When ${\rm dom}\,φ$ is a finite union of closed polyhedral cones, $f$ admits KL exponent $1/2$ for homogeneous quadratic pieces and exponent $0$ for nonnegative $φ$ that is linear on each cone. For any convex polytope $C$ containing the origin, we use the KL exponent $0$ to show that the full-step manifold proximal point iterates for minimizing the support function of $C$ over $\mathcal{S}$ stabilize at a critical point in finitely many steps.

title: AgentBank: Banking on Blockchain Agentic Payments
authors: Yuexin Xiang, Martin Perešíni, Yuchen Lei, Yuquan Li, Yuanzhe Zhang, Andreas Deppeler, Tsz Hon Yuen, Shiping Chen, Qin Wang, Burkhard Stiller
abstract: AI agents increasingly pay for data and computation through protocols such as x402 and AP2, but individually funded wallets idle and require asset transfers for every payment. We present AgentBank, a smart-contract banking layer that lets agents spend bank liabilities under owner-issued mandates and on-chain spending limits. Internal payments update account balances without transferring assets, while pooled backing funds are allocated between reserves and yield-bearing strategies. We bound losses from compromised agent keys and analyze how correlated demand affects reserve requirements. Experiments show that AgentBank reduces idle liquidity by 52-77% relative to per-agent wallets and lowers gas costs for batched internal payments. Using historical DeFi liquidity data, we evaluate how reserve policies balance treasury returns against payment availability during market stress. We further examine the risks of automated bank runs and evaluate mechanisms to mitigate them.

title: Can AI Design a Better nnU-Net? A Hypothesis-Driven Architecture Discovery Loop from Failures to Design Rules
authors: Songtao Jiang, Yuan Wang, Fucheng Niu, Hualiang Wang, Jian Wu, Zuozhu Liu
abstract: Neural architecture search and LLM-driven evolution often reduce evaluation to a scalar fitness score, discarding failures that could explain why designs succeed or fail. We present a hypothesis-driven architecture discovery loop in which LLM agents diagnose structured error patterns, formulate falsifiable hypotheses, test counterfactual controls under a frozen nnU-Net pipeline, and distill validated mechanisms into executable trigger-to-action rules. Across eight search waves, the loop identifies two principles for 3D medical image segmentation. First, reallocating computation from high-resolution decoders to the mid-encoder preserves thin-anatomy boundaries while reducing cost. Second, support-confined region contrast addresses errors between nested anatomical compartments, with anatomy-dependent triggers selecting when the rule applies. These principles produce LeanNeXt (0.78 MACs and 0.92 training-step time relative to nnU-Net; +1.63 Dice points on four-fold KiTS23 cross-validation) and trigger-routed LeanNeXt+. The latter improves all 15 evaluated CT/MRI settings over nnU-Net and exceeds the 3.3 larger ResEnc-M on 12 of 15 benchmarks at 0.30 its parameter count. Relative to random sampling, one-shot LLM generation, and score-selected agent search, the loop shows how failure analysis can yield reusable design rules across modalities.

title: Cancer multi-omics joint dimension reduction leads to reliable and interpretable survival predictions
authors: Vincent Le Goff, Vincent Guillemot, Cathy Philippe, Wiam Ahdidou, Gwendoline Mendes, Jean-François Deleuze, Edith Le Floch, Arnaud Gloaguen
abstract: Multi-omics studies are becoming more and more frequent, and are especially suited to decrypt the complexity of dysregulation happening in cancer. In this context, improving prognostication through interpretable methods could provide better patient stratification and help identify new prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Multi-omics data are however very often high-dimensional (few patients/high number of variables). A possible solution to high-dimensionality is Joint Dimension Reduction (JDR) methods, which compute a low-dimensional latent space from multi-omics data. In this work, we benchmark 12 JDR methods on 18 different TCGA cancer datasets. Survival prediction is achieved through a two-step process: the estimation of a low-dimensional multi-omics latent space followed by survival prediction with or without additional clinical data. We had to equip 4 methods with the ability to predict the survival of new patients. Results reveal that JDR methods can improve survival prediction with clinical data, and match the predictive performance of clinical data alone, with a high variability between different cancers. Among JDR methods, JIVE and RGCCA show superior performance. In a subsequent bootstrap analysis, JDR methods identify reliable prognostic biomarkers across cancers. We propose a clinically relevant interpretation of such markers on Low-Grade Glioma. Reproducible codes are available on https://github.com/vlegoff/MultiOBenchmark.

title: The Activity Geometry of Discrete Generative Sampling
authors: Xinlong Guo, Jie Zhang, Lingyou Zhou
abstract: Iterative refinement is a key capability of diffusion-based generation and has motivated growing efforts to bring similar behavior to discrete diffusion and flow models. A growing line of work enables such refinement by allowing previously generated tokens to be revised during sampling, thereby shaping the coupling between successive sampling states. Despite its growing role in sampler design, this coupling freedom remains insufficiently characterized. We introduce Activity Geometry to study these finite-step couplings through expected transition cost, which we call activity. We show that activity decomposes into the minimum required by the induced marginal transport and an excess term arising from the coupling. Using this minimum as a reference, we propose Minimal-Activity Finite-Time Coupling (MAFTC) to realize prescribed marginals with minimum activity without retraining or additional model evaluations. In the continuous-time limit, the minimum activity per unit time converges to the minimum expected jump rate compatible with the prescribed path. For metric-induced Gibbs paths, we further show that the activity of the kinetic-optimal flux admits a geometric decomposition. We find that total activity alone can obscure coupling excess: a sampler may approach the minimum activity required by the prescribed marginal transport while still retaining substantial coupling excess. In language generation, as the number of model evaluations increases, refinement-based samplers accumulate additional trajectory activity with limited diversity gains, whereas MAFTC reduces trajectory activity while maintaining comparable generation quality and higher lexical diversity.

title: Magnetoelectric response to a Néel domain wall in spin-orbit coupled superconducting films: Spontaneous currents, vortex pinning, and vortex-antivortex nucleation
authors: P. J. F. Cavalcanti, M. D. Croitoru, A. I. Buzdin
abstract: We study the superconducting response induced by a Néel domain wall in a thin superconducting film proximity-coupled to a ferromagnetic layer in the presence of interfacial Rashba spin-orbit coupling. The combined action of the magnetic texture and broken inversion symmetry generates a magnetoelectric coupling that induces spontaneous equilibrium currents. To establish the basic response to a continuously rotating magnetic texture, we first consider a periodic harmonic cycloid as an analytically tractable reference problem. Near Tc, this reference problem illustrates how the magnetoelectric coupling modifies the superconducting order parameter, while below Tc it provides a simple setting for describing the phase response, Pearl screening, and the interaction with a vortex. We then turn to the main problem of this work, a single Néel domain wall, and derive analytical expressions for its equilibrium phase profile, spontaneous current, magnetic field, and vortex-wall interaction energy.We show that the Néel wall acts as an extended magnetoelectric source and produces a vorticity-selective pinning landscape controlled by the competition between the wall width and the effective screening length. We further demonstrate that sufficiently strong magnetoelectric coupling can render a bound vortex-antivortex pair energetically favorable relative to the vortex-free state, even in the absence of an applied magnetic field. Our results provide an analytical framework for understanding magnetoelectric vortex pinning and vortex-antivortex nucleation by Néel domain walls in spin-orbit coupled superconducting films.

title: Metamorphic Testing of Learned Spatial Surrogates for Transit Accessibility
authors: Till Zacher, Markus Lienkamp
abstract: Transit-network design requires evaluating many candidates, but detailed accessibility calculations are too slow to repeat inside an optimization loop. We therefore train a neural surrogate to approximate them. Given a candidate bus network and fixed information about rail service and nearby opportunities, it predicts the calculated spatial change in accessibility. We compare its predictions with routing-derived targets in geographically held-out regions and test specified qualitative relations under controlled input changes. Reference calculations on constructed networks assess the applicability of relations that have a routing-level counterpart. Models with positive predictive skill can still fail basic connectivity tests. One targeted intervention substantially increases pass rates for two connectivity relations while predictive skill also improves. Average prediction error is therefore insufficient when a learned model becomes an optimization objective. Predictive agreement and controlled behavioral tests should be reported separately.

title: A characterization of almost everywhere convergence of subsequences of Walsh--Fourier partial sums
authors: Weisz Ferenc, Guangheng Xie, Dachun Yang
abstract: We characterize the increasing sequences $(ν_j)$ in the set of positive integers $\mathbb N$ along which the Walsh--Fourier partial sums $s_{ν_j}(f)$ of every integrable function $f$ converge almost everywhere to $f$. This resolves a problem that Konyagin posed in his invited address at the 2006 International Congress of Mathematicians~\cite{K06}. The criterion concerns the binary expansions of the integers $ν_j$. Divide each $ν_j$ by $2^k$. Convergence holds if and only if, for some $K\in\mathbb N$, the number of distinct positive quotients whose remainder has binary variation larger than $K$ is bounded independently of the scale $k$. This is also equivalent to the weak type $(1,1)$ inequality for $\sup_{j\in\mathbb N}|s_{ν_j}(f)|$, and if the criterion fails, then the partial sums of some integrable function along $(ν_j)$ are unbounded at every point. The criterion contains the bounded variation condition and Konyagin's condition for separated spectra, and we give examples, for convergence and for divergence, that are not covered by the earlier results.

title: Implementation of Machine Translation for the Uzbek Language Based on Transformer Models
authors: Mukhammadjon Musaev, Mannon Ochilov
abstract: This research focuses on building a machine translation system for the Uzbek language using transformer models such as T5 and mT5. Because of the limited data and the complexity of the Uzbek language, we collect, preprocess and augment data to create a strong Uzbek-English parallel corpus of about 3 million sentence pairs.
